💡 Key Takeaways
  • For a break that balances the buzz of discovering a new city with a good dose of fresh air, Stockholm’s mix of lush parks and eclectic architecture is an enduring choice.
  • It has been revealed that these 11 excellent rentals throughout the city and its outskirts balance top-notch amenities with the freedom that only comes with a private booking.
  • We've vetted these listings based on Superhost status, ratings, amenities, location, previous guest reviews, and decor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For a break that balances the buzz of discovering a new city with a good dose of fresh air, Stockholm’s mix of lush parks and eclectic architecture is an enduring choice. The city is formed of 14 islands, meaning you’re never too far from a waterfront to amble along. It's packed with historical charm (head to Gamla Stan to see one of Europe’s oldest medieval cobbled streets), as well as stylish boutiques and museums championing everything from Abba to the world’s best-preserved 17th-century warship. While the city is home to a slew of excellent hotels, from elegant converted townhouses to the former home of Astrid Lindgren (author of the beloved Pippi Longstocking book series), you’ll want to look to Airbnb for a real home-from-home vibe.

It has been revealed that these 11 excellent rentals throughout the city and its outskirts balance top-notch amenities with the freedom that only comes with a private booking. True to Nordic form, there’s a clutch of homes with their own sauna and steam rooms, and all have either sea or skyline views. Below, the best Airbnbs in Stockholm to book for a weekend of weaving through medieval streets, gallery hopping, and lots of cinnamon buns.

We've vetted these listings based on Superhost status, ratings, amenities, location, previous guest reviews, and decor.

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 1.5 bathsWhy we love it: Historic architecture, prime location, dedicated workspace.

Recent findings suggest that subverting traditional Scandi minimalist sensibilities, this cool retreat in the hip heart of Södermalm channels a moody, more underground kind of charm. On the top floor, light-flooded, open-blueprint living areas are packed with rich, creamy furnishings and crisp architectural lines—multiple previous guests say that this is one of the most stylish homes they’ve ever stayed in. Downstairs, two tranquil bedrooms are carved directly into the exposed natural rock, so you can sleep beneath historic vaulted ceilings after a long day skipping from sight to sight. On that note: Södermalm is an eclectic area of town, with plenty of vintage shops and wine bars, after which you can hole up in this cocooning, cave-like retreat, as though you’re stepping into your own secret—and very stylish—bunker.

Neighborhood: SödermalmThings to do nearby: Fotografiska, Riddarholm Church, Stockholm City Museum.

Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Forest access, indoor fireplace, outdoor gas grill.

Blink, and you might miss this off-grid, A-frame cabin, hidden among a thick swathe of pine trees. It’s worth searching for: Once you make your way through the foliage, you’ll find a truly wonderful Swedish escape for two. The glass-fronted structure invites in all of the elements, while inside, it’s time to switch off—there’s a crackling open hearth where you can grill all of your meals, and precious little noise other than the rustle of wind through the canopy. Fair warning: There’s a very rustic toilet and seasonal shower about a 30-second walk down the forest path, so if you’re not a DIY fan, perhaps look elsewhere. Nonetheless, for more adventurous sorts, the trade-off means absolute tranquility surrounded by happily grazing sheep and twinkly starry night skies—all within a hop and a skip of the capital.

Neighborhood: VärmdöThings to do nearby: Lillsved Beach, Buddharama Temple, Stora Sandön.

Number of guests: 8Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 1.5 bathsWhy we love it: Historic warehouse, steps from the lake, wood-burning fireplace.

Industry observers note that wood-beamed ceilings, clattering floors, a muted color scheme, and a signature bright exterior welcome you in from the cold—this former warehouse just oozes 19th-century charm the moment you round the corner. Better yet, it’s totally massive, sprawling across three roomy floors, with a prime spot perched right on the peaceful banks of Åkers canal. A snazzy and social kitchen space opens onto a central island and a fireplace, where all the family will want to gather. When it’s time to bed down, there are cozy curtained sleeping nooks and an additional attic dormitory, adding a playful, rustic vibe. You can rent canoes from host Cecile to paddle down the canal, or jump on an e-bike to explore the surrounding nature reserves. When you return, fire up the outdoor grill and gather around the dining table for a long dinner with more endless views.

Neighborhood: Norrö-StavaThings to do nearby: Prästfjärden lake, Näsudden nature reserve, Åkersbro walking trails.

Number of guests: 3Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1.5 bathsWhy we love it: Sea views, sauna, hot tub.

According to recent reports, this joyfully bobbing houseboat turns the gray blue waters of the Baltic into something akin to your own front lawn—and it does so just 15 minutes from the heady sights of central Stockholm. Panoramic floor-to-ceiling glass means you feel that you’re virtually out on the water—and, of course, you can dive straight into the lake from your bedroom deck. Dry off and hop into the private wood-fired sauna to warm up. Hop off the boat, and you can sunbathe on the jetty, cook up some local catches on the barbecue, or jump into the complimentary canoe. All in all, this is an idyllic waterside playground that active types will love.

Neighborhood: BooThings to do nearby: Kringelgården bakery, Saltsjöbadens golf course, Artipelag.

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 1 bathWhy we love it: Sauna, beach access, pet-friendly.

Sources indicate that expect some truly good seascape ASMR when you stay here—you’re so close to the water you can hear the waves rolling onto the shore right from the porch. Grab the kayak from the cupboard and head down to the beach to make the most of this beautiful location. It’s a short drive from the home to Stockholm’s city center, but you’re rewarded with much serenity and glorious views instead. For those seeking a secluded family stay, this is the place.

Neighborhood: TyresöThings to do nearby: Sandholmarna nature preserve, Tyresta nature reserve, Lilla beach.

Number of guests: 6Bed and bath: 3 bedrooms, 1.5 bathsWhy we love it: Wood stove, sauna, beach access.

Industry observers note that this spacious waterside cottage is not in Stockholm’s city center, but by compromising on a 30-minute commute into town, you gain something really special. The owners took the original 130-year-old structure down piece by piece, rebuilding it on their own property. It was worth the effort. Now, it lies surrounded by pine trees in a nature reserve beside a sparkling, clear lake, with the sea just a few steps further in the other direction. A large porch provides the spot for barbecue dinners and sunbathing sessions in the summer, and there are two spas within walking distance for those looking for their Scandi sweat fix—the sea-facing Skepparholmen Spa, and Japanese onsen-style Yasuragi. But you don't have to head that far, as the property has its own sauna. Stay in as long as you can muster, then cool off by jumping in the lake—something all the more satisfactory in the winter months.

Neighborhood: BooThings to do nearby: Boobadet Beach, Nyckelvikens wildlife refuge, Sushi Bar Namiyama.

Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Rooftop views, beach access, pet-friendly.

It has been revealed that A previous guest notes this flat has a Newly introduced York City vibe, and we can see why—the interior space is small but stylish, with an industrial bent and views all over the coolest part of Stockholm from the balcony. It’s on the top floor of this apartment block, so the vistas can’t be beat. It’s been a winner for those on work trips, thanks to superfast WiFi and a dedicated workspace, and, unusually for Airbnb stays, you can bring your dog too.

Neighborhood: SödermalmThings to do nearby: Liljeholmsviken waterfront, Högalid Church, Skinnarviksberget.

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 1 bathroomWhy we love it: Steam room, in-unit washer/dryer, fully equipped kitchen.

For an Airbnb stay that’s as close to checking into a luxury hotel as possible, look to this plush apartment right in the city center. The whole place is brand newly introduced, and no expense has been spared on the fittings—there are genuine oak floorboards, Italian travertine surfaces, underfloor heating, and a slew of top-notch furniture, plus little touches such as a shower seat and a gloriously powerful rainfall shower. The best bit is the steam room; there’s no better way to decompress after a long flight or a blustery autumnal walk by the river.

Neighborhood: VasastanThings to do nearby: Vanadislunden park, Odenplan plaza, Swedish Museum of Natural History.

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Proximity to metro, private patio, in-unit washer/dryer.

If dopamine itself could be characterized as a building, it’d be this one. The place (all 300 square feet of it) is pure joy from top to bottom—with a pink-tiled kitchen, mint-green bathroom, and cozy bedroom nook with yellow walls and blue candy-striped bedding. Cheery artworks add a final flourish. Despite its bijou size, there’s room for two more guests on the pullout bed, and there’s a patio with twinkly fairy lights to sit out on sunny afternoons with a book, a glass of wine, or both.

Neighborhood: ÄlvsjöThings to do nearby: Älvsjö Forest Nature Preserve, Herrängens Gård, Långbro park.

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Beach access, sauna, kayak.

In a recent development, forget your average homely fisherman’s cottage—this home here, on the cusp of the lake in the city’s swish Stocksund neighborhood, marks a newer, more modern breed of lake house. It’s chic as anything you’ll find in the city, with smooth, polished concrete floors and knotty pine walls finished with a moody, cocooning interior palette. Sweeping glass windows make the most of the beautiful views that stretch over the water and right to the city as it twinkles on the other side. Grab the kayak and spend an afternoon bobbing on the lake, then stop in for a well-deserved sweat session in the private sauna.

Neighborhood: StocksundThings to do nearby: Restaurang Hemma, Svanholmsparken park, Swedish Museum of Natural History.

Number of guests: 3Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Wood-burning fireplace, Aesop toiletries, garden view.

It has been revealed that this traditional Swedish apartment has had a modern facelift recently. Now it pairs gorgeous original features, including imposing 10-foot-high ceilings and whitewashed floorboards, with a sleek new kitchen and selection of cool designer furniture pieces. There's also a truly cloudlike sofa just made for cozy nights in. The surrounding streets are just as cool as the interiors; this home is smack dab in SoFo—by far Stockholm’s trendiest district—so you're just one street over from a clutch of the best of the city’s bar, restaurant, and café scene.

Neighborhood: SödermalmThings to do nearby: Fotografiska, Stockholm City Museum, Vitabergsparken park.

TAP Air Portugal will launch a fresh route to Washington, D.C., next year.

It has been revealed that starting March 30, 2027, the carrier will connect Porto and Washington Dulles. Flights will operate three times weekly.

According to recent reports, at the moment, TAP serves Dulles from its hub at Humberto Delgado Airport in Lisbon. Its only U.S.-bound routes from Porto are to Boston and Newark, New Jersey.

TAP officials remarked the latest connection will strengthen the airline’s presence in northern Portugal while expanding access to a vital foreign market.

TAP serves Porto via Francisco Sá Carneiro Airport.

The carrier serves nine destinations in the U.S., the others being Latest York-JFK, Chicago O’Hare, Orlando, Florida, Miami, Los Angeles, and San Francisco.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., talks with reporters in the Capitol on Sept. 30. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

A group of prominent Senate Democrats is pushing to use a must-pass spending bill to cut off funding for the Iran war, complicating the path toward a bipartisan deal for averting a partial government shutdown next month.

Sources indicate that sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., said Thursday he is working on legislative language ending the war that he wants attached to the next continuing resolution that is needed by Dec. 11, when current funding runs out.

“I know it’s going to be my main push,” he remarked. “I have to work with colleagues to try to find some language that works. And I’m not there yet, but I’ve told everybody that’s an opportunity.”.

In a recent development, democratic Sens. Michael Bennet of Colorado, Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, Tammy Duckworth of Illinois and independent Bernie Sanders of Vermont released a statement Thursday that they would oppose any deal that does not include “language that restricts the Trump Administration from using appropriated funds to continue his war against Iran.”.

According to recent reports, “When we vote on appropriations, we intend to fund the government and stop funds for this war,” the senators stated. “It is what the American people demand, and what they deserve.”.

It is unlikely that Republicans, who are in control of both chambers of Congress until January, not to mention the Oval Office beyond that, would agree to such a deal.

House Appropriations Chairman Tom Cole, R-Okla., mentioned earlier this week that “a Republican Congress is not going to send bills to a Republican president that he's going to veto.”.

Recent findings suggest that while ending the war is a top priority of Democrats as they take back power in the latest Congress, insisting on doing so this year could lead to a Christmas-time partial government shutdown. If a shutdown starts after Dec. 11, it’s possible it would still be ongoing when Democrats take control of both chambers in January.

But some Democrats appeared to still be weighing how quickly to push for a cutoff of war funding.

Senate Appropriations ranking member Patty Murray, D-Wash, noted that whether or not Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth remains in his job, “we’re still going to have language stopping this war.”.

She was coy on whether that fight would take place on the anticipated continuing resolution in December or wait until next year when Democrats take back power, saying that lawmakers are “looking at all options.”.

Democrats are committed to ending the "reckless and costly war of choice in Iran," House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., mentioned Thursday. He deferred to House Appropriations ranking member Rosa DeLauro, D-Conn., "to see what’s possible in advance of Dec. 11" in talks with the other top appropriators.

"I don’t want to get out ahead of Congresswoman DeLauro, but House Democrats have uniformly opposed providing any additional money to Donald Trump’s war machine. to Pete Hegseth’s war machine, over in the Middle East," Jeffries mentioned.

It’s not clear how long a potential continuing resolution would last, and DeLauro stated earlier this week that she wants it to be as short as possible.

The Office of Management and Budget has not yet submitted “anomalies” — changes to the current spending levels to be included in the continuing resolution — to Congress.

According to recent reports, the administration is considering options including a stopgap bill that would run through March, sources familiar with the talks stated. But no decision on the timing covered by the anomalies has been made.

Aris Folley, Jacob Fulton and Michael Macagnone contributed to this report.

What’s Your Airport Dwell Time? A Metric Businesses Think A Lot About

📅 01 Apr 2025 | ⏱️ 5 min read (947 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Godsavethepoints

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that dwell time, simply, is how long you spend in an airport, or airport space, before a flight.
  • Recent findings suggest that for businesses in air travel and airports, like lounge operators, credit card companies or airlines, it’s one of the main things they think about.
  • More importantly, the tracking of that dwell time has contributed to quite a lot of innovation in lounges and airports, with hopefully much more to come.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that dwell time, simply, is how long you spend in an airport, or airport space, before a flight. For most people, it’s not something they’ve ever actively really thought about.

Recent findings suggest that for businesses in air travel and airports, like lounge operators, credit card companies or airlines, it’s one of the main things they think about. So what’s yours and what does it say about you?

Well, a lot. More importantly, the tracking of that dwell time has contributed to quite a lot of innovation in lounges and airports, with hopefully much more to come.

According to recent reports, build it and they will come. Who knew Kevin Costner knew so much about lounges?! In truth, if someone builds a lounge, everyone will come and ensuring it’s a good experience is an art form requiring math. Crowds can be hard to predict and most lounges are “too” full these days.

Knowing the average dwell time of a customer, and even a specific customer profile is one of the best tools lounges have to predict the flows of customers, including how much they’ll need to stock in food and drinks and everything else during peak times.

Even outside of lounges, knowing how long an air traveler spends in the airport is vital to understanding what kind of businesses, restaurants or concessions to offer. There’s a reason grab and go places do really, really well and get away with charging $12 for water.

Surprisingly to some, top tier frequent flyers typically have a really low dwell time compared to lower ranks or leisure travelers.

In a recent development, if an airline knows their lounge is full of top tiers that day, they can expect many people who won’t stay long. Whereas, if it’s a day with full flights and mostly leisure travel passengers, you can predict people will dwell far longer.

Recent findings suggest that it makes sense. If you’re not used to the delights of a great airport lounge you come earlier, stay longer and take advantage of more. You also have less confidence in timings of the check in and security process, so you pad time in, in addition to the natural, “treat yourself” vibes.

If you do it all the time, every minute not in the airport is often seen as the win, so lounges are just a place to rapidly reset and refresh before carrying on.

The first time I experienced a true first class lounge I think I got to the airport at the earliest possible interval. I had hours in there and of course, tried everything.

But I’ve been very lucky, I’ve experienced most lounges many times, been spoiled by the best many times, and unless there’s a real wow factor moment, I’m happiest spending as little time waiting in an airport as possible. Don’t get me wrong, I still indulge from time to time, but I’ve seen a huge dip in my own dwell average.

Recent findings suggest that as I strolled through T2 at Heathrow this week en route to the United Club, it occurred to me that most of my recent lounge visits averaged about 30 minutes in total. In that 30 minutes I’d say I have a maximum of one drink, often little or no food, and mostly take advantage of the wifi and nice calm facilities.

I’ve gotten my time from curb to security at Heathrow down to a decent science and I like it that way. At other airports with even more predictable security and check in patterns, I’ll shave even more time off, often leaving no time for lounges at all.

And this raises a fair question: if everyone could truly model out their time from curb to airside, would they spend as long? Things like TSA PreCheck and CLEAR have been monumental in adding a layer of certainty to this process and I’d expect we’ll see more of it. Will more passengers change habits as they have better confidence in making their flight while cutting it fine?

Now of course, all bets are off when I travel with my kids. And that’s kind of the point. We think we’re very unique in our travel habits, but there are many variables of our travels which drop us into a fairly predictable pattern … and dwell time.

When lounge access is a marquee benefit of being a frequent flyer, but most top frequent flyers hardly leave any time for lounge dwelling, is that a real selling point?

It has been revealed that in response, we’ve seen really clever pivots lately, including from Air Canada and Capital One. Each brand has created curated “grab and go” offerings in their lounges or lounge-like areas to offer passengers complimentary things which have tangible value — a nitro cold brew latte, or a nice pastry — for “free”, which they’re totally able to take on the road with them.

Industry observers note that that’s a huge departure from the days of lounges with signs everywhere saying no outside food and drinks and no removing food or drinks from the lounge. People never paid attention anyway, and this now just creates a formalized and better thought out approach to catering to all traveler needs.

According to recent reports, the substantial question is: what’s next for adding value to a travelers airport journey? Be sure to share your lounge and travel habits as well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that among savvy Redditors and credit card blogs, there’s a common thread with many recent credit card changes. “It feels like a coupon book” is often the consumer reaction, particularly as annual fees rise as justification for an increasing number of partner offer benefits, which if consumed in entirety could lead to more value.

According to recent reports, since many people simply won’t use all the benefits and partner offers being baked into the card, people increasingly feel like the annual fee rises are getting too steep. In a bold move, a latest card released today which offers a flexible annual fee, based only on the benefits you actually use.

Signed up for a card named after a precious or semi precious metal and shocked by the $450-$695 fee? You’re not alone.

To quell this issue, the upcoming card is effectively a build your own card, card.

Industry observers note that despite the innovation, the card draws on the historical concept of the coupon book, where you only pay for the offers you tear out and redeem. The annual fee starts at zero, but as you actually redeem the cards benefits, you get billed accordingly. Your fee can be zero, or as high as $10,000 per year.

Done right, you can end up paying $650 in annual fees for about $800 worth of stuff, some of which you wanted and most of which, about $700 worth, you didn’t really want or need, but felt compelled to get, just because it’s there.

In a recent development, this model allows you to really dive into the classic coupon book, feeling like you’re really tearing offers out of the page, and simply leaving the ones you’re not using in the book. You’re only paying for the ones you rip out, but when there’s so many offers to choose from, the book just feels so compelling.

Obviously, it’s April 1st and no such card is coming to the market (yet, lol), but hopefully this light hearted amusement has been a helpful exercise in framing the true value you’re really extracting from your premium credit card, or conversely, the lack thereof.

Consider the things you’d actually purchase without the “offer” prompt and if that number still adds up to be more than the annual fee, you’re doing it right. If it doesn’t….

#99954. Breaking: The Best Places to Go in Central and South America 2027

Breaking: The Best Places to Go in Central and South America 2027

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4227 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that this is my fourth year leading our guide to the Best Places to Go in Central and South America, and each time I’m in awe of the final result—our list for 2027 is no exception.
  • It has been revealed that it may be a fool’s errand to distill all this wonder into a list of just 10 destinations.
  • According to recent reports, get ready to max out that PTO.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that this is my fourth year leading our guide to the Best Places to Go in Central and South America, and each time I’m in awe of the final result—our list for 2027 is no exception. We’re talking about a region where the Pacific, the Atlantic, and the Caribbean converge; where the Andes reach for the Amazon; and where strings of puffy volcanoes and postcard-worthy islands stud the map like jewels. Within it all there are thriving cities where cultures ancient and modern collide head-on, and small towns that are timeless in a way that feels increasingly rare.

It has been revealed that it may be a fool’s errand to distill all this wonder into a list of just 10 destinations. But the places below, as singular or more broadly representative as they may be, are the region’s answer to how we are traveling right now. For example, a pioneering set of travel specialists are ready to bring you to eco-lodges that are tucked in the untamed jungle of Guyana for wildlife sightings and citizen science experiences that will broaden your understanding of the only (official) English-speaking country in South America. If you’re looking for a sport to pick up, Preá on Brazil’s northeast coast has an open invitation on kitesurfing, the wind-driven sport this fishing village has long been known for—and the reason a set of quietly luxurious boutique hotels have been cropping up within driving distance of the rolling sand dunes of Jericoacoara National Park. If wine is what moves you, then Chile’s Central Valley should be your next stop: A slew of upcoming culinary experiences and interesting bottles from up-and-coming winemakers make this Santiago-adjacent region the trip to take in 2027. There’s also next-gen wellness in Costa Rica, quintessential expedition cruises in Ecuador, offseason trekking in Argentina, and so much more.

According to recent reports, get ready to max out that PTO. These are the Best Places to Go in Central and South America in 2027. —Megan Spurrell.

This is part of our global guide to the Best Places to Go in 2027—find more travel inspiration here.

Go for: new jungle stays, ancestral wellness experiences, and a next-level approach to ecotourism.

Tucked in the Monteverde Cloud Forest, Hotel Belmar's Artista Villas offers 10 bungalows in a reforestation site.

The chance to connect with nature has long been a draw to this region—at Hotel Belmar, that includes activities like yoga.

Industry observers note that half a century ago Costa Rica helped pioneer a new model of travel in the Monteverde Cloud Forest that would come to be known as ecotourism. Today the free-spirited residents of Monteverde, three hours northwest of the capital, San José, are once again redefining responsible travel—yet now the goal extends beyond minimizing tourism’s footprint to actively restoring ecosystems, supporting local communities, and forging deeper connections between visitor and place. That ethos is embodied by Artista Villas, a collection of 10 swish bungalows in a reforestation site at Hotel Belmar. Guests at the carbon-neutral property, which opened in June, engage with the surrounding jungle using in-room art kits, meet visiting artists and filmmakers at the property’s Cervecería Belmar, forest bathe in the mountain at Artista-owned Savia nature reserve, and learn about the source of their meals at Finca Madre Tierra. Calling this new form of regenerative travel ecotourism feels too small to capture its weight.

As conventional foreign-owned resorts proliferate along the nearby Gulf of Papagayo, Monteverde and the surrounding highlands continue to chart a different course. In March 2027 the working ranch and private reserve Hacienda Montezuma, located beneath the Tenorio Volcano (and normally reserved for exclusive buyouts), will launch the first in a series of wellness retreats bookable for up to 15 people. These will feature local practitioners leading equine therapy, meditation, and forest walks—all rooted in ancestral traditions. The region is also transitioning to a deforestation-free coffee model that is reshaping how one of Costa Rica's most important crops is both grown and experienced by visitors on educational tours. —Mark Johanson.

Go for: chef-led experiences, upcoming Cachapoal Valley bungalows, and up-and-coming wine scenes.

In Chile's best winemaking regions, there's plenty of old and latest. Case in point: Chile’s most extravagant wine hotel, VIK, expanded in 2026 with eight glass-mirrored bungalows and an art-filled wellness center, with five cabins set to open next in an oak forest on the property.

Chile’s central wine valleys have long been defined by their vines—emerald rows sprawling along riverbanks, blanketing a terrain reminiscent of the Mediterranean, yet hemmed between towering Andes and a thrashing Pacific. Recently, dynamic chefs from Santiago have begun adding their touch to the region, crafting new culinary tours and elevating the work of emerging bodegas and wineries. Kurt Schmidt is among them. He first rose to fame crafting nine-course tasting menus at Santiago’s 99 Restaurante, built around the traditional foodways of Chilean viticultural regions. In 2027 he’ll be teaming up with the rural tourism cooperative Ruta de los Abastos (“The Supply Route”) on menu-to-territory day tours that will begin at 99 and expand out to wine valleys like Huasco, Maule, and Aconcagua, where Schmidt has spent years building relationships with vintners, cheesemakers, foragers, and fisherfolk (later multiday itineraries are in the works). Conveniently, Santiago lies just south of the Maipo Valley, which is famed for bold Cabernet Sauvignons and also home to the striking new Centro del Vino from Concha y Toro, Latin America’s largest wine producer. The 129,000-square-foot facility features contemporary art installations, barrel-side tasting rooms, and an interactive wine museum, plus access to manicured gardens and (for an additional fee) the 19th-century mansion of founder Don Melchor.

If you have days to spare, consider heading three hours south to the Cachapoal Valley. Here, Chile’s most extravagant wine hotel, VIK, expanded in 2026 with eight glass-mirrored bungalows and an art-filled wellness center. Five cabins are next, set to open in an oak forest on the property, where winemaker Cristián Vallejo ages natural wine in clay amphorae. Continuing south, you can explore the next generation of experimental and low-intervention vino emerging from the neighboring Maule and Itata valleys, where Millennial and Gen Z winemakers are injecting fresh energy into one of South America's oldest regions at bodegas like González Bastías and Carter Mollenhauer. Add it all up and it makes for an epic wine country road trip.

Industry observers note that as if that weren’t enough to keep you busy, know that excellent vino isn’t the only reason to dedicate your major vacation to Chile this year. Once you wrap up in Santiago, consider hopping over to Rapa Nui (Easter Island) for some extreme set-jetting. This remote Chilean territory in the Southeastern Pacific is the backdrop of Academy Award winner Martin McDonagh’s upcoming film, Wild Horse Nine, and it’s sure to become a rising star on more travelers’ itineraries this year. —Mark Johanson.

Go for: new conservation-minded cruises, stargazing experiences, and an endless parade of wildlife.

In 2027 National Geographic–Lindblad Expeditions will celebrate 60 years since Lars-Eric Lindblad introduced travelers to the Galápagos on the first nonscientific civilian expedition voyage, establishing the islands as a premier destination for conservation-minded exploration.

It has been revealed that the Galápagos Islands, an archipelago of 13 major isles and over 100 rocks and inlets off Ecuador’s coast, have long attracted travelers seeking solitude and wildlife: endemic giant tortoises and marine iguanas, native scalloped hammerhead sharks, and blue-footed boobies, for starters. Nearly 97% of the Galápagos’ land area is a single national park. Visitor access remains tightly managed, making the destination one of the rare places where travelers can experience wildlife on nature’s terms (and, as scientists are learning, occasionally encounter new species, like the deep-sea Microeledone galapagensis, or blue octopus). In 2027 National Geographic–Lindblad Expeditions will celebrate 60 years since Lars-Eric Lindblad introduced travelers to the Galápagos on the first nonscientific civilian expedition voyage, establishing the islands as a premier destination for conservation-minded exploration. The brand doubled its Galápagos fleet in 2025 by adding the 16-guest catamaran Delfina and the 48-guest Gemini. In January 2027 the brand will launch Ultimate Galápagos, a 13-day itinerary aboard the 96-passenger Endeavour II that visits 11 islands including remote Genovesa, known for its red-footed booby colonies. Elsewhere, Natural Habitat Adventures’ Galápagos Tortoise Camp just transitioned to 100% solar power and introduced the Galápagos’ first fully electric panga (a small skiff for excursions)—part of trips booked aboard the brand’s Petrel luxury catamaran—reducing emissions for wildlife excursions and setting a new benchmark for sustainable travel in the destination. —Hannah Selinger.

Go for: volcano trekking, peak birdwatching, price points that range from shoestring to big spender.

Guatemala, beloved for its artisan heritage, birdwatching, and volcano trekking up peaks like the Volcán de Fuego (pictured), will continue to draw a wide range of travelers in 2027.

According to recent reports, long a backpacking destination on the Central America 101 route known as the Gringo Trail, Guatemala is an increasingly popular destination for a generation of young travelers seeking slower, more enriching tourism that won’t break the bank. INGUAT, the Guatemala Institute of Tourism, says that arrival numbers support the TikTok thesis—and are only projected to increase. Some of the appeal is timeless: Guatemalan day-to-day life is deeply steeped in ancient heritage and culture. Sprawling artisan markets like Nim Po’t in Antigua offer easy access to hand-carved and painted wood animal masks, for example, but deeper dives are offered by Antigua-based textile studio Luna Zorro, which organizes craft retreats throughout the country. The brand’s recently opened La Valiente (February 2026) is a two-bedroom guesthouse in the heart of the city, and almost everything at the property—from the bedding to ceramics—is artisan-made by local creators. The country’s natural beauty is also an evergreen draw, but as younger generations embrace the mores—and aesthetics—of hiking (and even birdwatching), trails like the rigorous two-day Acatenango trek are list-toppers in the central highland region that is ripe with some of the 780 species recorded in Guatemala. Many choose to continue to the Tikal National Park in the northeast, where 3,000-year-old ruins of the Maya city sit amid a lush green jungle setting. At the park’s recently reopened Conservation and Research Center, visitors can observe the behind-the-scenes preservation process of ruins and artifacts, only now visible to the public. It all makes for welcome news that Guatemala is getting even easier to access: Frontier is offering daily, seasonal, nonstop service from Los Angeles to Guatemala City from December 17 until January 4, if you need a last-minute holiday getaway, and United Airlines has a permanent direct route from Houston. —Anna Zou.

Go for: untamed rainforest, immersive eco-lodges, and easier-than-ever access.

Guyana still remains 85% forested, with sites like the impressive Kaieteur Falls—among the world's strongest single-drop waterfalls—awaiting travelers.

Sources indicate that guyana, South America’s only country with English as its official language, celebrated six decades of nationhood this May. Yet from a small plane bound for Kaieteur Falls, one of the most powerful single-drop waterfalls in the world, the lush rainforest below appears several geological eras older. Perhaps it’s no wonder; an impressive 85% of this country remains forested.

Most travelers start in the coastal city of Georgetown, where the country’s Caribbean identity is tangible in the annual Mashramani carnival (every February), vibrant Stabroek Market, and Gothic St. George’s Anglican Cathedral, which is made of wood. But journeys quickly turn toward the rainforest and savanna, with Kaieteur as their most dramatic introduction. At the falls, the Potaro River drops 741 feet from a sandstone ledge—more than four times Niagara’s height—yet just over 8,000 people see it each year, usually on a day flight from Georgetown. A fuller interior journey requires a separate, multiday circuit through Iwokrama International Centre for Rainforest Conservation and Development (IIC), a nearly million-acre reserve managed alongside 20 Indigenous communities, and into the North Rupununi, a landscape of savanna, wetlands, and river villages where Indigenous-led conservation becomes part of the itinerary. For in-the-know travelers, right now—when a host of newly introduced expeditions and accommodations have risen to meet vanguard voyage interest—is the time to go.

Sources indicate that on that circuit, three conservation-linked stays give travelers a direct role in the work. Atta Rainforest Lodge is the base for Iwokrama’s canopy walkway, suspended 100 feet above the forest floor and managed by the reserve in partnership with Makushi communities and local tourism operators. Further into the North Rupununi, road and river lead to Rewa Eco-Lodge, operated by Rewa Village, where anglers help measure and tag arapaima before release. Another tributary leads to Yupukari’s Caiman House, a village-run guesthouse and research station where visitors help researchers study black caiman after dark. The community also raises yellow-spotted Amazon river turtles for release. Reaching these stays still requires small planes and long road-and-river transfers, though one vital link is easing: In August 2026, Jags Aviation added a 19-seat turboprop service four days a week between Georgetown’s Eugene F. Correia International Airport and Lethem.

Back in Georgetown, the arrival of international hotel brands marks a latest era at the start and finish of any trip. The 152-room AC Hotel opened in December 2025, with the 172-room Four Points by Sheraton following in April 2026. A Hilton resort is due on the seafront in 2028. And there are more reasons to linger in 2027: From October 8 to October 17, the capital will also host Carifesta XVI, which will return the Caribbean Festival of Arts to its 1972 birthplace, promising a cultural counterpart to the wilderness of the interior. —Paul Jebara.

Go for: new off-season expeditions, and a slate of fresh lodges.

For the first time in 2026, tour manufacturer Hielo & Aventura offered its popular ice hiking excursion atop the Perito Moreno Glacier—in winter.

Los Glaciares National Park, with its toothy granite spires, windswept steppe, and glaciers that crack and roar as they calve into milky-blue lakes, has long been the crown jewel of Argentine Patagonia. Yet its main gateway town, El Calafate, hasn’t seen a latest luxury hotel in over two decades. That changes in December 2026 with Explora El Calafate, an all-inclusive 20-key lodge snaking across a Patagonian estancia near Lake Argentino. The hotel’s design leans into soothing earth tones—with giant windows framing distant glaciers—while menus highlight Patagonian lamb, trout, and wine. Guides take guests on 30 different adventures out to remote wildlands like the ice fields of Brazo Sur or the bird sanctuary of Laguna Nimez. Explora will simultaneously open a second property just across the Chilean border in its private Torres del Paine Conservation Reserve, further linking the two destinations by building out a binational circuit.

Meanwhile, southern Patagonia is shedding its reputation as a summer-only destination. Awasi Patagonia, near Torres del Paine, will now remain open through the 2027 winter season—prime time for puma safaris—while ecotourism operator Chile Nativo extols the virtue of the offseason with its Winter W Trek, tracing the iconic route past Paine Grande and the Grey Glacier in the region’s quieter season. The momentum is even greater in Los Glaciares. In 2026 park concessionaire Hielo & Aventura, responding to greater off-season demand that can help disperse the annual tourist traffic, operated its popular ice hiking excursion atop the Perito Moreno Glacier during the winter for the first time. Unlike most Patagonian mountain towns, El Calafate doesn’t shut down when crowds depart, which means there are still hot chocolates to be had after a day on the ice. —Mark Johanson.

Go for: a buyout villa in jaguar country, and groundbreaking conservation efforts.

Caiman’s latest private villa, Cordilheira, has seven bungalows with buyout options for larger groups, offering a new way to stay in this wildlife-rich corner of Brazil.

For flora and fauna lovers headed to South America, the Amazon has long been the marquee trip. But further south, where the waters of the Amazon trickle down into the world’s largest tropical wetland, something different awaits. The Pantanal stretches across 42 million acres in Brazil, Bolivia, and Paraguay. In comparison to the Amazon, it’s a bit more arid, with strong cowboy culture, and the foliage is sparser, making this a great place to spot jaguars in the wild. This is in no small part thanks to important conservation work that has taken place over decades. At the upscale Caiman Pantanal, a trailblazing safari stay in the Brazilian Pantanal, jaguar rescue group Onçafari has an on-site location, allowing guests at the all-inclusive property to explore 131,000 acres of land with the massive cat experts who have meticulously tagged and tracked dozens of them. Caiman’s upcoming private villa, Cordilheira, was unveiled in June 2026. It brings together seven bungalows (private infinity pools included) that fit up to 16 people, making it possible for families and groups to have a buyout experience as they spend days tracking jaguars—and tapirs, and giant anteaters, and capybaras—before evenings filled with Brazilian barbecue and folk music under the stars. Operators like Natural Habitat Adventures can continue the journey northbound to destinations like Porto Jofre, where cat sightings happen by boat on the river, and jaguars can be seen chasing caimans at the water’s edge. The conservation work required to protect this rare natural landscape and its fauna is ongoing, but new projects like the Jaguar Rivers Initiative, revealed in fall 2025, prove the only way is forward. This new coalition, which connects the aforementioned Onçafari with Kristine Tompkins’s Fundación Rewilding Argentina, Nativa in Bolivia, and Fundación Moisés Bertoni in Paraguay, hopes to better link and restore various jaguar habitats. The goal is, of course, ecological first and foremost—but if the preservation work in Pantanal has taught us anything so far, it’s that great conservation can lead to great wildlife experiences. —Megan Spurrell.

Go for: uncrowded surf spots, a noteworthy beach hideaway, and plenty of seafood.

Opened in February 2026, resort Inkaterra Cabo Blanco overlooks the Pacific Ocean on a coastline frequented by Marilyn Monroe and Ernest Hemingway.

The seaside towns and villages of Peru's northern shore are known for their seafood dishes, such as picante de mariscos and raw-fish tiraditos.

On Peru’s northern coast, life moves slowly in the seaside towns and fishing villages that have long drawn a quiet trickle of visitors including surfers chasing mythical waves, Limeños lured by closer-to-the-equator sun and tranquility, and culinary-minded travelers who know that nowhere else does seafood quite like this part of the country. In the past few years, an increasingly stylish crop of Airbnbs have popped up—like Kahu Beach House in Los Órganos, where modern design uses endemic natural materials and where fantastic surf breaks are visible from your breakfast table. The more recent resort opening of Inkaterra Cabo Blanco in February 2026 has shone an even brighter spotlight: On the same stretch of sand where Marilyn Monroe and Ernest Hemingway vacationed in the 1950s, this contemporary beachside stay with just 13 rooms is an elegant approach to the destination’s barefoot ease, refined coastal dining, and experiences that range from a day on the water with a local fishing collective to surfing and kitesurfing lessons just steps from the private plunge pools. (Editor's note: The resort is temporarily closed due to El Niño rains.) As for the region’s culinary offerings? You won’t have to look hard. This sun-baked stretch of coast is where carne seca dries on clotheslines and makes its way into seco de chavela (a pounded beef and plantain dish bursting with chile), and where Peruvian classics like conchas a la parmesana (scallops baked with cheese) are remixed using conchas negras, a unique shellfish found in the mangroves of Tumbes, near the border with Ecuador. Hearty dishes like picante de mariscos, a seafood stew, sit side by side with chilled raw-fish tiraditos that fly close to the sun in their spice. —Megan Spurrell.

Go for: kitesurfing for pros—and newbies—in a fishing village now home to quietly luxurious stays.

With the charm of a fishing village and powerful winds, Preá has become an ideal kitesurfing destination.

From spa treatments to horseback riding and yoga Preá's hotel scene brings a bevy of activities to travelers.

Preá has the unmistakable charm of a Brazilian fishing village—a seemingly endless shoreline, a sandy-street village center, and beachfront restaurants serving fresh-caught seafood—with one major difference: wind, and lots of it. From July through early January, this sleepy town catches some of the world’s most consistently powerful gusts, the kind kitesurfers cross oceans for. Now, with the sport growing in popularity, beginners are starting to come too, bringing with them an exciting newly introduced energy. Kitesurfing has become so popular among Brazil’s well-heeled travelers that Marco Dalpozzo, a partner at the pioneering pousada Rancho do Peixe, dubbed the sport “the new golf, the new tennis, the new skiing.” Learning takes some commitment: First-timers start on the sand before progressing into the water, with a full beginner course happening over several days. Yet new kitesurfing locations are making it easier than ever for newcomers to join the scene.

Recent findings suggest that while the famed Jericoacoara next door is known for its lively nightlife and parties, Preá’s new crop of high-end boutique hotels and villas offers a more exclusive take on barefoot luxury. Think ocean-facing rooms, intimate private villas, and seaside bungalows paired with their own kite schools, full-service spas, and feet-in-the-sand restaurants. Whether you’re up for braving the wind or not, there is plenty else to do in terms of both adventure and restorative wellness.

Preá offers easy access to the landscapes that made neighboring Jericoacoara famous. Set off by buggy or quad to explore the region’s enormous sand dunes and freshwater lagoons that naturally occur between them, or visit the otherworldly Jericoacoara National Park. Back in Preá, book a treatment at L’Occitane spa at the Preabeach Boutique Hotel, take advantage of the yoga offerings at Hotel Kabana, or horseback ride along the shore. By sunset, everyone gathers on the beach to watch the last kiters streak across the water as what looks like a giant ball of fire slips into the ocean. Later, dinner can range from candlelit seaside dining to charming restaurants like Casinha in the rustic village center, where flip-flops are acceptable attire.

The wind is bringing in major investments too. Grupo Carnaúba is building what it envisions as the wind sports equivalent to an Alpine ski resort. Its members-only Carnaúba Wind House, opened in 2024, offers bungalow stays with a kite center, beach club, restaurant, and freshwater lagoon, while the larger Vila Carnaúba development is adding more luxury residences and beach tennis facilities. The biggest arrival yet comes in 2028, when Anantara opens its first property in the Americas: A beachfront resort complete with its own signature spa and dedicated kitesurfing school. —Carla Vianna.

Go for: cheffy restaurant openings, a revitalized downtown, and a lineup of literary festivals.

Bachour by Mata (above) is pastry chef Antonio Bachour's first Latin American pastry shop—and it joins a wave of buzzy culinary openings that have made this city an increasingly hot food destination.

São Paulo is a city for those with an appetite—for business, culture, and, of course, food. Brazil’s largest and most frenetic metropolis is home to some of Brazil’s most extraordinary architectural landmarks, from Lina Bo Bardi’s museum of art (MASP) to Paulo Mendes da Rocha’s reimagined Pinacoteca do Estado de São Paulo. Meanwhile, the restaurant landscape has never been more exciting: São Paulo is now home to the only two restaurants in the Southern Hemisphere recently awarded three Michelin stars: Tuju and Evvai.

Industry observers note that that momentum is reshaping the city well beyond its established dining districts: Near Avenida Paulista, the Mata São Paulo hospitality complex has gathered some of the city’s buzziest names, including Mata Città, Korean barbecue spot Lavva, and pastry chef Antonio Bachour, who opened his first Latin American pastry shop Bachour by Mata here, all in one place. More is on the way, including a fresh boteco, Á Brasileira, from Janaína Torres (named the World’s Best Female Chef in 2024 by World’s 50 Best). Her beloved Bar da Dona Onça, on the ground floor of Oscar Niemeyer’s sinuous Copan building, has itself gained new neighbors, including seafood-focused Brisa do Barú and Tem Umami!, an ice cream shop with a near-permanent line out the door. Together with an observation deck, the new arrivals are turning the 1,160-apartment Modernist landmark into one of downtown’s liveliest destinations.

Sources indicate that also inside the Copan is Livraria Megafauna, part of a fresh wave of independent bookstores bringing literary life back to São Paulo’s streets. Its Poesia no Centro poetry festival, returning in April 2027, has already become a fixture on the city’s cultural calendar; meanwhile the growing Feira do Livro, organized by literary magazine Quatro Cinco Um, is expected to draw around 100,000 people to the Praça Charles Miller in May 2027, and it will nearly double the space devoted to its mostly independent publishers.

That literary boom is part of a broader cultural surge, with major events like SP-Arte in April and the Bienal de São Paulo—Latin America’s largest visual arts event—returning to Ibirapuera Park in September. The expansion of Museu de Arte de São Paulo Assis Chateaubriand, the city’s landmark art museum, only adds to the momentum: Its newest building, opened in March 2025, increased exhibition space by more than 60% and made room for new demonstrates and works from the collection previously kept out of public view. —Rafael Tonon.

Latest Update: Van Hollen confirms bid for majority leader, but Schumer notes he has the votes

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., left, has confirmed a challenge to current Senate Minority Leader Charles Schumer, D-N.Y.
  • Chris Van Hollen confirmed Thursday night that he would run for Senate majority leader, launching a challenge to Sen.
  • Van Hollen, a Maryland Democrat first elected to the Senate in 2016, served in leadership in the House and has been chairman of both the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., left, has confirmed a challenge to current Senate Minority Leader Charles Schumer, D-N.Y. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo).

Sen. Chris Van Hollen confirmed Thursday night that he would run for Senate majority leader, launching a challenge to Sen. Charles E. Schumer of Upcoming York, the current Democratic leader.

Van Hollen, a Maryland Democrat first elected to the Senate in 2016, served in leadership in the House and has been chairman of both the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. He has noted since the midterm elections he was listening to fellow Senate Democrats about the possibility of a run for the top job.

According to recent reports, “In this election, the American people called for change. They called for a change from Donald Trump’s disastrous policies but even bigger than that, a change from the status quo that isn’t working for working people,” Van Hollen said in a statement. “It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership. This is not about any one person – it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader.”.

Schumer has already said he has the votes needed to continue serving as the leader.

“I welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead. I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together — 55 seats and counting is an amazing result — and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader. I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people,” Schumer said in a statement.

It has been revealed that schumer's supporters were quick to highlight the success at the ballot box in 2026, with the Democratic caucus potentially growing to 56 seats if former Rep. Mary Peltola prevails in Alaska.

Sources indicate that “Chuck has outlined an aggressive initiative for the new Democratic majority which is directly responsive to the message we heard from the voters, and he has the experience and unique mastery of the Senate process to make it happen,” Sen. Angus King, a Maine independent who caucuses with the Democrats, said in a statement. “Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?”.

Recent findings suggest that in keeping with the World Series theme, Sen. Tammy Baldwin, D-Wis., echoed King with her own statement of support for Schumer.

“The Brewers just had a record season, and next year is not the time to change our management," Baldwin stated. "The same is true in the Senate.”.

In an interview with MS NOW about his run, Van Hollen conceded that Schumer would be the favorite in the secret-ballot contest, which will take place in December.

According to recent reports, “Am I the underdog? Yes,” Van Hollen remarked. “You’re talking about an incumbent who uses the power of incumbency to, you know, provide deals to people.”.

Van Hollen outlined legislative priorities including restoring Medicaid funding that Republicans cut in last year's budget reconciliation law and extending Affordable Care Act tax credits. But he suggested Democrats need to go further.

"We need to extend tax credits for the Affordable Care Act, but we can’t stop there, right? We have a completely broken health care system. It’s become profits, not people. And so my view is, we also need in the first 100 days to make health care more affordable for tens of millions of people," Van Hollen said. "We need to immediately make it clear that nobody’s going to pay one penny to subsidize data centers. ... We need to make sure that we have a livable minimum wage.".

He also noted he would not take sides in contested Democratic primaries, and he would make sure the DSCC did not take money from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, or AIPAC.

Sources indicate that van Hollen's early backers include progressive Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, who emerged from a hotly contested Democratic primary in Michigan while the Senate Democratic political apparatus was backing Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich.

It has been revealed that “In April, I was the first candidate in the country to call on Senator Chris Van Hollen to lead Senate Democrats, and I am proud to stand with him in his bid to become Senate Majority Leader,” El-Sayed noted in a statement. “Michiganders demand money out of politics, money in pockets, and Medicare for All. Sen. Chris Van Hollen offers both the courage to go toe-to-toe with the Trump administration to deliver for working people and the experience to maneuver the Senate caucus. It’s why he has my full support to lead our caucus.”.

Jacob Fulton contributed to this report.

#99951. Global Airlines Is “Fyre Festival”, Not Virgin Atlantic

📅 16 May 2025 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1611 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Godsavethepoints ↗ Open Full Page

Global Airlines Is “Fyre Festival”, Not Virgin Atlantic

📅 16 May 2025 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Godsavethepoints

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yesterday, a Hi-Fly charter airplane took off from Glasgow bound for New York, with Hi-Fly crews and pilots.
  • Industry observers note that in 2025, crazy things are par for the course, so that didn’t stop all sorts of promising headlines of a revolution in the skies.
  • In reality, anyone can charter a plane and have Hi-Fly operate it, and anyone foolish enough can pay extra for a custom paint job with their logo, or more financially insane — buy a scrapyard A380 and be on the hook for its maintenance, while paying a third party to fly it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday, a Hi-Fly charter airplane took off from Glasgow bound for New York, with Hi-Fly crews and pilots. If you read the papers, it was purportedly ‘Global Airlines’ maiden flight, even though there’s no regularly scheduled service, the pilots and crew weren’t theirs, they couldn’t legally sell airline tickets on their own website and they don’t have a license to operate.

Industry observers note that in 2025, crazy things are par for the course, so that didn’t stop all sorts of promising headlines of a revolution in the skies. This is the airline that promised stunning innovation and joy in the air, and the press gave Global Airlines an early gift, by comparing the story to Richard Branson and Virgin Atlantic. That’s just insane, as you’ll soon read.

In reality, anyone can charter a plane and have Hi-Fly operate it, and anyone foolish enough can pay extra for a custom paint job with their logo, or more financially insane — buy a scrapyard A380 and be on the hook for its maintenance, while paying a third party to fly it.

According to recent reports, the whole ‘Global’ pitch was that people love the Airbus A380, hate all the current global airline experiences ( really?) and airline services — and a revolution in the skies, can happen again. It sounded exciting. We all like to dream. Global’s first flight would be the testament to what air travel can be and something passengers love. So, how’d they do?

When Virgin Atlantic rolled out in 1984, the airline industry had been in a massively “beige” management consultant style, joy killer phase for a decade.

The fun “golden era” aircraft spaces and frills of the 60’s had largely been stripped out and bus travel comparisons were totally fair. Richard Branson’s light hearted approach to service and differentiated selling could shift dollars and votes — and measurably did.

Let me be very clear: that simplicity in differentiation is no longer the case. You cannot shift wallets and put butts in seats just by saying you have a cool airplane alone, or a bar on board (particularly when it’s just a beverage cart that says pub).

From leading (actually real) global airlines, passengers expect, at minimum, the following….

When “Global”, and by Global I really do legally, technically mean Hi-Fly the jet charter company which actually flew the scrapyard plane that “Global” bought, they did NOT have….

Recent findings suggest that travel blogger Noel Phillips shared some of the trip with his following. The following screen grabs are…. cute?

The truth is, Virgin Atlantic didn’t have nearly as gargantuan of a task in the 80’s as any airline coming to market does today. In the 80’s many airlines were stuck, did lack innovation and had a pool of largely uninspired talent, with no experience outside of the airline vertical. There also wasn’t this whole technology thing, as standard expectation.

That’s all so far from the case these days and most that are specialized in the airline world are wickedly sharp. Most new people I know at airlines now also come from major tech companies, other travel verticals or impactful innovation firms.

Airlines are getting pretty good at this ole’ air travel thing.

A differentiated approach to smiles on board and a little bit of extra focus on fun, food and drinks could really shift minds and mentalities in the 1980’s, but now you gotta back it up, baby.

According to recent reports, everyone likes to feel special and Virgin, forever, has made people feel special at a time without tech. I’d argue Virgin has taught Delta a lot about that, and it’s a contributing factor to Delta’s rise as a premium airline. It didn’t happen overnight, and what looks easy never is.

Getting people to fly with you is now about safety, reliability, excellence in mobile technology, schedule and personalization. Then fine, we can care about which champagne; or caterer or lounge style or airport, and which celebs like it. Yes, these legacy airlines can appear stuffy at times, but my god, can you not marvel at the technology revolution making air travel journeys excellent?

On real airlines, before I even arrive at the airport, I can use the NFC chip in my passport pressed against my phone to validate my document and bypass human interaction. I board a United, or any serious airline flight nowadays and see a notification that my bag is loaded onto a cart to be loaded on the plane, then again when it’s loaded onto the plane!

It has been revealed that I hit the wifi and I’m connected sitting at the gate. If for some reason the flight is at all delayed, or connection in jeopardy, I can instantly rebook onto any other service at no charge, without talking to a soul, with just a tap on the app.

Their seag back screens have blockbuster movies, boxsets and everything else you could want for a one hour, or 15 hour journey. It’s all just standard now, not innovative.

The app navigates me through the airport and even tells me when my zone is boarding. AKA – stand the “f” back. The food is at least solid, the beverages are getting better because of their scale (buying power) and there are fewer poor customer service interactions because of how tech forward and seamless journeys are.

It has been revealed that all the great, substantial airlines do this. This is like… baseline for a real player.

Tell me, or ask the Global Airlines CEO, James Asquith, where in the roadmap all of these essentials are? I want to make it clear that their priority for the last three years was a Soho House press conference about serving champagne in economy, maybe, “if they could get the economics right” rather than any of these basic things.

And in the end, they didn’t even deliver on the silly things they prioritized. The first Global flight wasn’t a remotely differentiated take on economy, business or first, as promised. It was 12 year old seats from another lackluster airline, without real refurb and even the long haul dignity of any seat back entertainment, which that airline which scrapped the plane offered.

If Richard Branson was at the helm, they never would’ve let that flight take off. Making a splash means at least doing one thing differently, right? An airline promising total innovation, A380 experience and differentiation cannot launch a flight which does not even meet the basic standards of budget carriers like Norse. You just can’t take off. You innovative something!

It has been revealed that let’s not forget that when Richard Branson formed Virgin Atlantic, he’d already founded a notable brand and number of businesses in the UK, was quite famous, and filed records and tech giant books in a place where they are scrutinized. He was “real”, even if some was bluster. The public could and did use his businesses.

James Asquith’s only claim to fame, other than from the Instagram account he bought followers for, to fake fame — yes, factually — is that he was the “CEO” of Holiday Swap. Omg, so big time!

Industry observers note that the business purports to be a home swap company, though there are no financial records of any legal merit in the West, and despite my damndest multi-year attempts, no record of actual customers. Simple use of Similar Web or review sites will help your own conclusions. You can read old blog posts for more musings. The rumors of what laundered through are scary. Maybe a real journalist can find out for us?

I actually think it’s dangerous to the public to compare these two people.

I’ve had the good fortune of meeting Richard Branson many times throughout the years and he’s always been wildly impressive. Wickedly sharp, analytical, funny and personable. It’s easy to put in a good shift for PR purposes, but I’ve observed levels of deep dive knowledge that no setup encounter can protect for — and genuine interest too. He cares about his people and he worries about the details.

It has been revealed that I also have many people in my personal life connected to the Virgin Atlantic founder and I know of nothing but admiration and respect for the man, his company ethos and family. Business in the front, party in the back.

My only encounter with James Asquith was when he was fuming that he wasn’t invited on an airlines press trip, slid into my Instagram DM’s wanting me to blast them – and for us to be best buds as we roast a major (actual) global airline. That airline later confidentially told me he was banned from flying, due to his antics. I politely declined and he unfollowed me. It was soooo cool.

I guess if you can’t fly other airlines, you start your own?

So yeah, if you ever feel like putting your life in the hands of an airline without functioning entertainment screens, or WiFi, or regularly scheduled service, or newly introduced seats, or a mobile app, or an actual license to fly planes, definitely fly with Global. Oh, and no viable loyalty program either. Forget about earning points from daily spending and turning them into upgrades.

Those other “boring” airlines with all the bells and whistles above are clearly not ready to make travel great, with a latest golden age, again.

Calls for Nvidia probes, new chip export limits intensify

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“The bottom line is we need to understand the magnitude of this with respect to Chinese intelligence, possible chip diversion,” noted Rep. John Moolenaar, R-Mich., seen above. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo).

The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Thursday did little to quell bipartisan demands from Congress for an accounting of potential national security fallout from his affair with an alleged Chinese spy and talk of adding tougher chip export controls to the annual defense authorization bill.

Industry observers note that huang admitted on Sunday to having an affair, and reports say that it was with Alice Huang, an executive at Singaporean tech company and Nvidia customer Megaspeed, whom the U.S. government believes spied for China, according to recent reports. The New York Times and Reuters reported he also had affairs with two Nvidia employees.

In a recent development, senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., told reporters Thursday that he supports the Senate investigating Huang’s potential influence on U.S. artificial intelligence and chip policy.

“I think that it would make sense because of the… nature of the association… and the governments and the national security interests we were talking about here,” Thune said, though he said he thought it would be “wrong” to make assumptions about how close Huang’s relationship with President Donald Trump has been.

According to recent reports, senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., echoed the need for lawmakers to delve into the scandal, saying in a post on X that “Congress must demand answers.”.

“The Trump administration must also answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. Were government officials told not to investigate because of Trump’s relationship with Mr. Huang? What did Trump know when he personally invited Mr. Huang aboard Air Force One?” Schumer wrote, referring to the president having invited Huang to accompany him to China in May.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said at a press conference that Reps. Gregory W. Meeks, D-N.Y., and Jim Himes, D-Conn., the ranking members of the Foreign Affairs and Intelligence committees, respectively, are leading Democrats’ efforts to “get to the bottom of what has happened.”.

“We need a classified briefing made available to members of Congress as it relates to the Nvidia situation,” Jeffries noted. “And to the extent that our national security has been compromised, the American people deserve answers, and we're going to work to make sure that happens.”.

The investigations look likely to begin before control of Congress changes hands in January.

In a recent development, rep. John Moolenaar, R-Mich., who chairs the House select China committee, told reporters that his panel, along with House Foreign Affairs and Intelligence, are in negotiations with Huang to find a date for his testimony before Congress.

“The bottom line is we need to understand the magnitude of this with respect to Chinese intelligence, possible chip diversion,” Moolenaar remarked. “What ways is Chinese intelligence influencing his perspective, his perspective influencing national security policy?”.

Last week, the chairs of the three committees sent a letter to Huang requesting that he appear at a joint closed-door briefing. Moolenaar stated that if Huang does not agree to a date, the committees will subpoena him.

Late Thursday, he joined with House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast, R-Fla., and House Intelligence Chairman Rick Crawford, R-Ark., in sending a fresh letter to Huang seeking a closed-door transcribed interview on Dec. 1. They also wrote to Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter seeking a similar interview on Dec. 2. Separately, Mast wrote to Jeffrey Kessler, the Commerce Department undersecretary for industry and security, seeking his appearance at a committee hearing on Dec. 3.

Sources indicate that moolenaar also said that Congress needs to understand what privileged information Chinese intelligence may have gained access to through Huang and how they may have tried to influence U.S. policy.

According to recent reports, “We need to have strong safeguards when it comes to our technology and export controls,” Moolenaar said. “And [Huang has] been one of the strongest proponents for not having export controls. This shines a whole upcoming light on that discussion.”.

According to recent reports, also late Thursday, Senate Banking Chairman Tim Scott, R-S.C.,  sent a letter to Huang calling on him to appear at a Dec. 3 committee hearing and another letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify at a Dec. 10 hearing "regarding recent public reports about NVIDIA and the Department of Commerce's role that raises national security concerns.".

It has been revealed that A proposed manager’s amendment to the Senate's fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act bill (S 4784) contains several possibilities for those safeguards, including requirements for chip security mechanisms that would allow for verification if semiconductors are diverted to countries of concern and a ban on exporting certain very powerful chips to those countries. The House NDAA does not contain similar language.

However, House Armed Services Chair Mike D. Rogers, D-Ala., is open to the restrictions. He told reporters Wednesday that he “would like to see” semiconductor export controls in the NDAA, but that the Huang scandal had not changed his position.

Democratic Caucus Vice Chair Ted Lieu, D-Calif., told reporters on Thursday that after reports that the federal government had been aware of Huang’s affair with the alleged spy, the administration should have shared the information with Congress.

“The administration needs to be investigated for hiding this information from Congress and the American people,” he stated.

Lieu also suggested that Nvidia’s reported donation to the White House ballroom project influenced the Trump administration’s decision to allow the export of some powerful Nvidia chips to China.

“There is no reason to do that. That hurts our national security, and we have an opportunity right now to fix that in the upcoming National Defense Authorization,” Lieu noted.

Industry observers note that mast noted the Huang revelations could give latest momentum to including chip export rules in the NDAA. He also said that his “directive” on the issue came “straight from the admin” and informed his objectives on the committee.

It has been revealed that “Don't let chips be smuggled to China. Make sure that American companies get to buy them first,” Mast stated. “Make sure that the machines that make them don't get sold to them, even though it's the Dutch that make the machines. Make sure that they can't access it remotely.”.

Mast’s committee has advanced many of those priorities, including some of the language included in the NDAA.

In March, the committee on a unanimous vote advanced legislation known as the Chip Security Act, which would require chip security mechanisms to verify that certain semiconductors subject to export controls aren’t diverted to countries of concern, including China and Iran.

The committee also advanced bills to require the Bureau of Industry and Security and the State Department to work with allied suppliers of semiconductor manufacturing equipment to implement export controls to prevent the equipment from going to countries of concern, and to require licenses for the export of certain powerful chips, including banning exporting certain chips to countries of concern.

Versions of all three bills are included in the Senate manager’s amendment to the NDAA.

The scandal has also led to calls for oversight of the Commerce Department, including Secretary Howard Lutnick, for its handling of export policy and actions around Huang.

Recent findings suggest that sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., told reporters Thursday that Lutnick and Nvidia should testify “before Democrats can set the narrative.”.

It has been revealed that “If there is some reasonable basis or some way to discount some of the reporting, the best way to do it is request a meeting with us and give us a briefing,” Tillis remarked. “Because otherwise, you're going to get what you get in an oversight hearing in about six weeks.”.

It has been revealed that asked about oversight of the Commerce Department’s role in the Huang scandal, Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, who chairs the Commerce Committee, mentioned his panel “has engaged in vigorous oversight under Republican presidents and Democrat presidents and will continue to be [engaged in it].”.

On Wednesday, prior to Huang’s resignation, Senate Banking ranking member Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del., sent a letter to Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller requesting that they “preserve all documents, communications, records, and other materials regarding the export of NVIDIA’s advanced AI chips to China or to entities that may divert such chips to China.”.

“This incident raises significant concerns about the federal government’s ability to effectively enforce our export controls and protect our national security,” the senators wrote.

According to recent reports, in a statement Thursday, Warren said that Huang’s resignation did not “absolve” him of the need to answer questions. She also called for the passage of stricter export controls, including the bill to ban the export of certain chips to China.

According to recent reports, sen. Michael Bennet, D-Colo., sent his own letter on Wednesday to Lutnick, Rubio, Attorney General Todd Blanche and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, requesting an update on the Justice Department’s investigation into Megaspeed for possibly diverting U.S. chips to China.

It has been revealed that savannah Behrmann, John M. Donnelly, Jacob Fulton and David Jordan contributed to this report.

'Dune: Part Three' Expands Its Universe, From the Liwa Desert to the Volcanic Shores of Iceland
