📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that on Location peels back the curtain on some of your favorite films, television indicates, and more.
  • It has been revealed that the celestial saga that is Frank Herbert’s Dune was practically made for cinema.
  • On December 18, 2026, Denis Villeneuve’s Dune: Part Three arrives, overcoming the hurdles that had tripped up its predecessors and capping off the decade-in-the-making trilogy in an explosive finale.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that on Location peels back the curtain on some of your favorite films, television indicates, and more. This time, we take a look at Dune: Part Three.

It has been revealed that the celestial saga that is Frank Herbert’s Dune was practically made for cinema. And yet, for so long, adapting the breathtakingly expansive space opera seemed like something of a curse. David Lynch called his turn at the franchise “a huge, gigantic sadness” in his life, and for Alejandro Jodorowsky, his psychedelically expensive vision for Dune never escaped development hell.

On December 18, 2026, Denis Villeneuve’s Dune: Part Three arrives, overcoming the hurdles that had tripped up its predecessors and capping off the decade-in-the-making trilogy in an explosive finale. Key to the creation of the trilogy’s universe was keeping it as grounded as possible in ours, with otherworldly planets raised from the volcanic shores of Iceland’s beaches and the banded dunes of the United Arab Emirates’ Liwa Desert. By this point, fans of the first two installments are well-acquainted with settings like the desert planet of Arrakis, but Villeneuve's latest offering delves deeper than ever into their intricate textures. Condé Nast Traveler spoke with production designer Patrice Vermette, location manager Duncan Broadfoot, and director of photography Linus Sandgren to learn how this much-anticipated conclusion was crafted.

Dune: Part Three opens with Fremen forces landing on Enfeil, a wetland planet that stuns the soldiers—used to desert and drought—with its rain. After the battle concludes, the Fremen forces run to the black sand shores of the planet and wade into the sea. This sequence was filmed in Iceland, specifically at Ingólfshöfði Beach, a nearly 250-foot-tall cape and nature reserve. “Denis [Villeneuve] always envisioned a black surface going on for forever, a super flat surface with those low clouds and a band of light, just the sun piercing through the horizon," remarked Vermette, “Because of the black sand, we thought, obviously, Iceland. We also looked to see if it was possible to shoot in the Canary Islands.” At the end of the day, Iceland won the booking, leading the team to spearhead an unprecedented film shoot. “When we scouted Iceland, there were multiple options,” said Broadfoot, “but this particular beach that we ended up on is part of a nature reserve, and actually during the summer, you can book puffin tours, but it's never been shot on before, so that was also an appealing aspect.”.

According to recent reports, twenty different locations across the UAE's Liwa Desert were stitched together to comprise Arrakis. Across all three films, the Liwa Desert has been used as a stand-in for the desert planet at the center of it all. “There's a reward to travel to the Liwa Desert, which is close to the border of Saudi Arabia, and the dunes there are like the kind you've seen in Lawrence of Arabia,” mentioned Sandgren, “it's magical just to be there; they're beautiful and contain copper sand and beige sand, and the mix of the two creates these incredible patterns of ripples from the wind each night, and every morning, you see upcoming patterns.” While Sandgren arrived at the desert for the first time to film for Part Three, for Broadfoot and Vermette, returning to the region was like a homecoming for the crew. “Denis [Villenueve] and Patrice [Vermette] are always very keen to find something new that we haven't filmed on before, so that was always the challenge," said Broadfoot, “specifically for Part Three, we had to go deeper and further into the desert than we had done in Part Two.” Filming in the ever-shifting landscape with temperatures peaking at a boiling 120 degrees Fahrenheit posed significant challenges to the shoot, especially as the crew based themselves even deeper into the desert, but getting comfortable was almost counter to the brief. “We love making movies because we thrive on challenges, you know?," said Vermette, "If it was easy, I don't think we'd want to make them.”.

In a recent development, while nearly all of the Arrakis scenes were shot in the Liwa Desert, select sequences were set in Al Ain, the UAE's “Garden City.” Though scenes shot in Al Ain didn't take up as much screen time as those shot in the desert, they span a considerable range as the area served as the setting for Alia Atreides's personal Golgotha—the site where Paul's sadistic younger sister crucifies traitors to the regime—as well as where Chani plays with her young children. “It's an incredible area that is still very unknown,” mentioned Vermette. “We shot on a mountain called Jebel Hafeet, the only real mountain in the area,” said Broadfoot, “we scouted the entire mountain and found a plateau up high, which gave you this sort of scale and rocky, craggy environment that's very different than the desert which we were filming in. It was a blank canvas for Patrice [Vermette] to take over and create his beautiful set.”.

To enhance all the footage that was shot on location, several landscapes from Part Three were recreated using a combination of practical and digital effects across four facilities in Budapest: NFI Studios, HungExpo Budapest Congress and Exhibition Centre, Korda Studios, and Waberer. Much of the battle scene on Enfeil was shot in Budapest. “Most of it was in the back lot of Waberer,” stated Vermette, “the amazingly technical thing achieved by Denis [Villeneuve] and Linus [Sandgren] was that they erected a 65-foot-tall by 470-something-foot-long LED screen wall, which was the biggest wall of that sort ever built." The sheer scale of the shoot even required the crew to break out cranes to navigate the airspace around production to move props and equipment around.

Atreides home planet Caladan has made an appearance in all three films of the trilogy. The visual opposite of Arrakis, Caladan was shot on the northwestern Kråkenes region of Norway. The agrestic shoreline is hugged by verdant cliffs and the frosty Norwegian Sea. Caladan's cameos in Part Three come as brief flashes, but Vermette also winks to the filming location in an Easter egg on Arrakis. “In the movie, in the interior courts of Alia's meditation room, there's a tree,” notes Vermette, “I had the idea of putting a pine tree, a Norwegian pine tree there, because it's the roots of their family; it's something that anchors their family. The only pine tree in all of Arrakis is right there.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that this week, Virgin Atlantic celebrates 25 years of flying to India.
  • On the sidelines of the IATA Annual General Meeting, basically the UN General Assembly of airlines, the new strategic partnership for India was announced with very interesting nods to the future.
  • IndiGo carries more passengers in India than anyone else and will connect US and UK/European customers flying Virgin, Delta and Air France KLM onward in India, while also helping fill seats for these European and North American partners, as their own customers head West.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that this week, Virgin Atlantic celebrates 25 years of flying to India. In Virgin fashion, it’s doing so in style, with a joint announcement among partners Delta Airlines, Air France-KLM, and a upcoming strategic partner IndiGo.

On the sidelines of the IATA Annual General Meeting, basically the UN General Assembly of airlines, the new strategic partnership for India was announced with very interesting nods to the future.

IndiGo carries more passengers in India than anyone else and will connect US and UK/European customers flying Virgin, Delta and Air France KLM onward in India, while also helping fill seats for these European and North American partners, as their own customers head West.

That’s probably a good thing, because with recent service additions, Virgin now flies a million seats a year to India and it sounds like others are piling on more flights too. It’s now one of the largest operators to India.

According to recent reports, I’ve been bullish on India as the next great center of the world for a while now. It’s not necessarily that I’m at all intelligent, it’s just based on the fact that India is the world’s largest population. But, when Ed Bastian, Delta’s formidable CEO notes it, people tend to listen. Bastian mentioned India being the most important aviation market globally now and signaled a return of direct services for the carrier as well.

Virgin has been a small step ahead, adding service regularly on their Delhi, Mumbai and Bangalore routes. IndiGo chose this alliance over formidable competition and this will certainly be a space to watch as more global airlines and alliances focus on India.

According to recent reports, geo-political activity points to India becoming a fresh manufacturing super power, in addition to its prolific work in tech, IT and customer service, not to mention blossoming tourism. These kind of globally connected businesses are massive business, huge in fact, for corporate contracts and easy onward connectivity to regional sites is essential. The partnership makes sense.

Recent findings suggest that in a somewhat rare and impressive signal of unity and seriousness towards India, Virgin Atlantic made their India crews part of the core Virgin family, rather than as contractors through a third party local tech giant, known in aviation world as a GSA. This means Virgin’s India crews are a part of the full team, with benefits too.

It has been revealed that when asked about loyalty implications of the latest alliance, Virgin Atlantic CEO, Shai Weiss, noted a mutual passion for using loyalty to enhance guest experience far beyond just the earn and burn of points and miles. For future iterations, they’ve offered the following….

The MoU (memorandum of understanding) also creates a framework for deeper collaboration between the carriers on a bilateral and multilateral basis; contemplates commercial collaboration including network, loyalty, cargo and sales, subject to regulatory approvals; explores areas of non-commercial cooperation including aircraft maintenance, sustainability, training, ground handling; and acknowledges the need to develop advanced collaboration through use of technology to efficiently service joint customers.

IndiGo will provide onward connectivity for Virgin and the other strategic partners to 32 destinations, making it easier than ever to see Udaipur, Jaipur, Mumbai, Kashmir and delights further south in Bangalore and Goa.

I just returned from the lovely Leela Palace in Delhi, as I watched the news happen live.

To me, India is a country of joy. Even people with truly nothing seem to find positivity and it’s generally a way of life here. Hospitality is as warm and steeped in tradition as it comes, too. It’s hot, it’s humid, but it’s an experience unlike any other and that’s something that’s harder to say these days than I’d like.

It has been revealed that the food, ugh. I adore. Sure, I’ll take a dosa from the South over a heavy curry from the North most days, but I love both and if you don’t love a good black daahl there’s something wrong with you.

Sources indicate that in short, it’s already fairly easy to get to India but it’s about to get a whole lot easier and not just to hub cities too. More seats means more chances to use points, by the way!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

JetBlue is growing its presence in Central America and the Caribbean.

According to recent reports, for the first time ever, the carrier will serve the Honduran capital of Tegucigalpa. Starting Feb. 25, 2027, flights from Fort Lauderdale, Florida, will arrive at Palmerola International Airport in Comayagua, which serves Tegucigalpa.

Currently, JetBlue’s only destination in Honduras is San Pedro Sula, in the country’s northwest.

According to recent reports, on Feb. 23, the carrier will launch service between Fort Lauderdale and George Town, Grand Cayman, in the Cayman Islands.

Both routes will operate daily, using a mix of Airbus A320 and A220 aircraft.

JetBlue will also offer limited-time daily service from Fort Lauderdale to Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago, between Jan. 29 and Feb. 15. The connection will help travelers reach the islands during Carnival, the airline stated.

“We’re grateful for the way customers across South Florida continue to embrace JetBlue, and we’re committed to delivering even more of the destinations and travel options they’re looking for,” Daniel Shurz, JetBlue’s senior vice president of revenue, network, and enterprise planning, said in a news release. “With new international service to Honduras and Grand Cayman, we’re strengthening Fort Lauderdale’s role as a key gateway to Latin America and the Caribbean, making it easier for customers to reconnect with loved ones, explore new places, and travel across our growing network.”.

American has prioritized Latin America as demand from U.S. markets, especially Miami, grows. The carrier just recently debuted service to Barranquilla and Cali in Colombia and will add Barcelona, Venezuela, to its network in January.

Legislative Branch bill would hold off on GAO cuts

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (604 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A group of visitors walks past the Capitol on Sept.
  • With stopgap funding set to expire in less than a month, Senate Republican appropriators Thursday unveiled a roughly $5.3 billion draft fiscal 2027 Legislative Branch spending bill that would boost security funding and sidestep contentious debates over a key watchdog.
  • The proposal would provide $965 million for Capitol Police, a nearly $83 million hike from fiscal 2026, but still short of the more than $1 billion the department requested as threats against lawmakers rise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A group of visitors walks past the Capitol on Sept. 22. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call file photo).

With stopgap funding set to expire in less than a month, Senate Republican appropriators Thursday unveiled a roughly $5.3 billion draft fiscal 2027 Legislative Branch spending bill that would boost security funding and sidestep contentious debates over a key watchdog.

The proposal would provide $965 million for Capitol Police, a nearly $83 million hike from fiscal 2026, but still short of the more than $1 billion the department requested as threats against lawmakers rise.

In a recent development, and it would bump funding for the Government Accountability Office up to $860 million, an increase of nearly 6 percent from fiscal 2026. That stands in contrast to the version of the bill advanced by the House Appropriations Committee in May, which floated slashing the GAO by 25 percent.

It joins several other draft spending bills released this week by Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, who is trying to kickstart bicameral negotiations as lawmakers stare down a Dec. 11 deadline to fund the government.

Her committee ran into a stalemate on topline numbers earlier this year that stopped it from marking up any of the 12 annual bills, but lawmakers nipped the threat of a government shutdown in the bud ahead of the midterm elections by pushing through a continuing resolution. With that funding now set to expire next month, appropriators are hoping they can wrap up at least some of the bills while punting the rest into the next Congress with another stopgap.

Sources indicate that the Legislative Branch bill is the smallest of the 12 appropriations bills and typically among the least controversial. But debates over the GAO have become a sticking point during the Trump administration as the agency accuses the White House of violating budget laws — a move the Office of Management and Budget has pushed back on, arguing the GAO has no authority over the administration since it is part of the legislative branch.

The GAO has been without a permanent head after its longtime leader Gene L. Dodaro retired last year, although Republicans are now making a last-ditch effort to get one confirmed during the lame-duck session before Democrats take power.

Sources indicate that the House version of the spending bill sought to bar the comptroller general from suing under the 1974 budget law restricting presidential impoundments, unless specifically authorized by Congress. But the Senate proposal includes no such language, and overall, it appears designed to avoid drastic or contentious moves.

It would also leave in place a provision that would block cost-of-living adjustments for members of Congress, whose pay has been frozen since 2009.

Senate Democrats, however, criticized the bill text after its release, saying it wouldn’t invest enough in the legislative branch.

“The Legislative Branch bill underfunds key work to support oversight of the Executive Branch, and it underfunds crucial efforts to keep the Capitol complex safe,” Senate Appropriations ranking member Patty Murray, D-Wash., noted in a statement.

The Architect of the Capitol would get $762.5 million, though funding for House office buildings is not included in that total. The agency is requesting $1.6 billion as it seeks to begin large-scale renovations of the Rayburn House Office Building. The architect has repeatedly warned lawmakers that parts of the Capitol complex are in need of critical infrastructure upgrades, arguing that delaying renovations will only make them more expensive as things continue to deteriorate.

The bill’s $5.3 billion proposal represents funding for the Senate and legislative branch agencies, while excluding House-only funds, which are typically added later.

  • I’ve sailed on more than 80 cruises, sometimes with my kids, often surrounded by everyone else’s.
  • Recent findings suggest that A cruise line that devotes a day to all things LEGO and offers a special baby laundry service gets top marks in my list of the best cruises for kids and teens.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the best cruise lines for families with kids and teens are likely more diverse than you realize. Many are the significant-ship brands you see in ads, tricked out with waterslides, dazzling shows, and an abundance of onboard restaurants to satisfy picky toddlers and ravenous teens alike. Yet other family-friendly cruise lines let mom and dad get the taste of luxury they crave or provide the entire crew with adventure and active pursuits around the globe.

I’ve sailed on more than 80 cruises, sometimes with my kids, often surrounded by everyone else’s. I can tell you that the best family cruises won’t make bedtime any easier, but they will do their best to make sure no one in your crew ever feels the need to cry, “I’m so bored!”.

Recent findings suggest that A cruise line that devotes a day to all things LEGO and offers a special baby laundry service gets top marks in my list of the best cruises for kids and teens. MSC Cruises is a European big-ship cruise line that’s making waves in the US with its family-friendly mega-ships.

According to recent reports, five kids clubs for babies, preschoolers, kids, tweens, and teens target activities to different age groups. MSC is constantly developing latest family programs, including family discos, original game shows, drone races for teens, MasterChef at Sea cooking challenges, and obstacle course competitions.

According to recent reports, world Class ships feature the top-deck Family Aventura District with an outdoor adventure area (including an overwater swing ride), water park, and an indoor space for rollerskating and bumper cars. Select ships offer arcades with a Formula 1 simulator and virtual reality attractions or the Robotron robotic-arm thrill ride. The line’s US–based ships also feature connecting cabins and family-friendly dining (the pizza and gelato are superb).

Families looking for an exclusive hideaway can book rooms in The Yacht Club, with access to a private restaurant, lounge, sun deck, and pool—all ages welcome.

Standout itinerary: 7-night Caribbean and Bahamas cruise on MSC World America sailing round-trip from Miami.

Royal Caribbean operates the world’s largest, most activity-laden ships, and its calling card is high-energy fun for all ages.

Sources indicate that families can rock climb, zip-line, ice skate, splash down waterslides, solve escape room challenges, and enjoy entertainment ranging from musical performances to acrobatic high-dive dance highlights without leaving the ship. The enormous Icon Class ships even have a dedicated family deck called Surfside, where kid-friendly restaurants, splash playgrounds, and a carousel are surrounded by cabins and suites designed to accommodate families.

Recent findings suggest that on all ships, parents can steal away for adults-only fun when they drop the littlest cruisers at onboard nurseries run by professional caregivers. Kids can make crafts, play games, and do science experiments at onboard camps operating morning until late in spacious, tech-enhanced multipurpose spaces. Teens have their own hip hangouts for foosball, video games, and evening parties with new friends. The whole family can later reunite to share the day’s fun over Johnny Rockets burgers and shakes or perhaps a teppanyaki dinner with showman chefs.

Standout itinerary: 7-night Perfect Day CocoCay and Caribbean cruise on Icon of the Seas sailing round-trip from Miami.

Disney’s rapidly expanding cruise ship segment isn’t just for preschoolers reveling in their Frozen era. Its itineraries across the Caribbean, Alaska, and Europe offer family fun for a wide range of ages, including adults. Plus, its short itineraries pair nicely with a theme park visit.

Entertainment is a highlight, from live on-stage productions of classics like Moana and Beauty and the Beast to mealtime shows themed around the Marvel universe and Coco. The ships’ movie theaters screen first-run flicks across the Disney-owned studios (not just animated classics), and the once-a-cruise Pirate Night is the only time you’ll ever see fireworks launched from a cruise ship.

It has been revealed that disney Cruise Line’s enormous youth facilities, also with nurseries and teen clubs, offer activities themed to Disney IP. Kids can design a superhero suit or theme park ride, pilot the Millennium Falcon, and join Olaf for virtual snowball fights. The line also treats adults very well with pools, sun decks, fine-dining restaurants (including ones by Michelin-starred chefs), bars themed around The Haunted Mansion and Star Wars, and cafés exclusive to travelers ages 18+.

Recent findings suggest that disney supports traveling families in less flashy ways, as well. Cabins feature extra berths for kids, split bathrooms with a toilet in one room and a sink in the other, and room-dividing curtains so grownups won’t distract would-be nappers. Waiters will purée baby food and cut up your kid’s dinner all while cracking silly jokes and performing magic tricks. When the travel logistics are handled, families can focus more on having fun.

Standout itinerary: 4-night Bahamas cruise on Disney Wish sailing round-trip from Port Canaveral.

Retirees rule the world of river cruising, but AmaWaterways has teamed up with Adventures by Disney (Disney’s escorted travel arm) to offer select Rhine and Danube cruises to families.

Disney’s onboard Adventure Guides handle all the logistics in port, from escorting tours in every destination to managing dietary restrictions and directing guests to the best restaurants and local treats. On board, they host movie evenings and kids-only dinners so parents can enjoy a leisurely meal with adult conversation.

Adventures by Disney swaps the history- and culture-focused walking tours typical of river cruise excursions for alpine coasters, amusement parks, river kayaking, and visits to chocolate factories. A selection of winery visits and slower-paced tours appeal to multigenerational families willing to split up childcare responsibilities ashore.

AmaWaterways, in turn, has specially built ships with more third-berth and connecting cabins than the typical river ship. It supplements its regional cuisine with kid favorites, while introducing the whole family to specialties like French macarons and German sausages.

Standout itinerary: 7-night Rhine River cruise from Basel, Switzerland, to Amsterdam, Netherlands.

It has been revealed that A family cruise can be a nature-filled adventure to places like Alaska, the Galápagos, Baja California, Iceland, Greenland, and even Antarctica. For active families with curious kids and teens (and parents!), National Geographic-Lindblad Expeditions is a top choice.

It has been revealed that the cruise line’s ships carry under 200 guests, so families can focus on each other without those big-ship distractions. Though small, the ships do offer connecting cabins to accommodate groups and casual dining with plentiful options to suit all tastes.

On a National Geographic cruise, the destination is the draw, and family-friendly activities range from snorkeling and kayaking to hiking and biking. On select voyages, the cruise line offers its National Geographic Explorers-in-Training program for kids and teenagers, led by certified field instructors. The program focuses on nature, science, and storytelling, with activities like practicing smartphone photography in Alaska with a photo instructor, collecting and then observing plankton under a microscope in Baja California, and learning to drive a Zodiac.

Standout itinerary: 7-night Galápagos Escape cruise from Quito, Ecuador.

Luxury cruise ships aren’t built for kids, but select cruise lines make an effort to entertain junior cruisers during holiday and summer sailings in places like Alaska and the Caribbean. Regent Seven Seas Cruises’ ships might not offer a dedicated kids club on board, but the line’s longstanding Club Mariner Youth Program welcomes children ages 5 to 17 with a schedule of onboard activities.

It has been revealed that trained counselors make use of the ships’ public spaces to keep kids busy with mini-golf games, dessert decorating, karaoke parties, and movie nights. In Alaska, programming is destination-themed, and a youth-oriented enrichment speaker engages kids in learning about Alaska’s nature and wildlife.

Don’t underestimate your family’s ability to find fun on an adult-oriented ship. On Regent, kids can enjoy swimming in the onboard pool, joining a team for trivia, and playing board or card games in the library. Afternoon tea and evening demonstrates may also become family attractions. You might find that complimentary room service from the main dining room menu coupled with movies on-demand in your suite is the perfect family activity to end your day.

Standout itinerary: 7-night Alaska cruise on Seven Seas Explorer from Vancouver, Canada, to Whittier, Alaska.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s June, and for perhaps the first time in modern history, Santorini isn’t crowded.
  • And that’s a shame, because there’s been a lovely tourism revolution brewing there, where local hoteliers are bringing back the kind of experience and hospitality that you want to come back for over and over again.
  • As someone who goes at least once or twice a year, and will again very shortly, I can only advocate to tick it off the bucket list this summer, because you’ll never find prices, availability or an experience quite like it again for a while.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s June, and for perhaps the first time in modern history, Santorini isn’t crowded. Those earthquakes a good few months ago? Not even a flower pot was tipped over, yet incessant clickbait headlines managed to have a lasting impact.

And that’s a shame, because there’s been a lovely tourism revolution brewing there, where local hoteliers are bringing back the kind of experience and hospitality that you want to come back for over and over again.

As someone who goes at least once or twice a year, and will again very shortly, I can only advocate to tick it off the bucket list this summer, because you’ll never find prices, availability or an experience quite like it again for a while.

In the last 20 years, Santorini got totally overrun. Cruise tourism and day trip mania somewhat ruined a once idyllic, low-key fishing island and then Instagram and TikTok lit the match.

But now the TikTok crowd is in Mykonos and Santorini, as unequalled in beauty as ever, is lovely again. Hotels like The Vasilicos and Santorini Sky bring wildly different, delightfully luxurious and hospitality driven experiences to the island.

Recent findings suggest that beach clubs, yes Santorini’s beaches are underrated, have made a nice little mark on quieter coasts with great effect too. Assyrtiko, the local grape has hit the world stage as a darling of sommeliers in top restaurants and vineyards like Vassaltis offer stunning tasting experiences.

And the food? There’s no Nobu, or Scorpios here, so there are plenty of places to feel the benefit of European pricing, including a personal favorite at Kantouni.

The trouble with Santorini has historically been that many of the best hotels are small, they fill up rapidly, and as they do, they charge a fortune. For the best, like the ones mentioned above, it’s still worth it. But this season, all across the board, prices are lower and even if you don’t care about price, many of the best which might typically be sold out for the season have rooms.

Recent findings suggest that as an additional tailwind for travelers, flights between the US and Europe are quieter this summer, which means there’s deals to be had with both points and cash from major markets to Santorini. If you don’t see cheap flights to Santorini, try a major hub and booking an onward ticket separately.

In a recent development, naturally, precaution is a good thing in life. But fear mongering for the sake of clicks is another beast and I can’t help but be fairly appalled by the many weeks and months of coverage and follow up coverage, reiterating a narrative of fear… despite no damage to anything, anywhere.

If you do bag a great deal this summer and visit one of my very favorite places, and use this great Santorini guide to make the most of your time, you can thank the media.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that my favorite thing about San Juan? You can have a morning that feels plucked out of a history book, an afternoon that commits you entirely to the beach, and a night that’s topped off with a frosty Medalla, sweet rum cocktail, and flirty bachata dance. It’s glitzy yet lush, historic yet ever-evolving, a city delightfully full of contrasts, and one I will never run out of reasons to revisit.

My father’s side of the family is from Puerto Rico, so I’ve been coming back to the island for years, and I love that there’s always another corner to get to know. There’s Old San Juan, with all its pastel-painted façades, galleries and shops, blue cobblestone streets, and tucked-away restaurants; Condado and Ocean Park for long, sea-salty afternoons by the ocean; and Santurce, where street murals, galleries, haute dining, and a lively bar scene bring a fresh, creative vibe to the city.

Of course, there’s no shortage of hotels in San Juan, but sometimes a vacation to the island’s capital calls for a little more room to sprawl, or a front door that opens onto a lush little neighborhood rather than a buzzy hotel lobby. The city’s best Airbnbs offer just that, along with wonderful amenities, whether it’s a private pool hidden behind swaying palms or a breezy courtyard for sipping on some local morning coffee.

Consider this your invitation to soak up the sun in Puerto Rico's capital for a few days. Read on for nine of the best Airbnbs in San Juan to consider for your next trip.

  • Sources indicate that sources said Trump is planning to nominate Eric Ueland, who currently serves as deputy director for management at the Office of Management and Budget.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., speaks during a Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee business meeting on Sept. 23. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Republican leaders have skipped a bipartisan deliberative process for recommending the next comptroller general to head the Government Accountability Office, as lawmakers prepare to consider a nomination for the post from President Donald Trump.

Sources indicate that sources said Trump is planning to nominate Eric Ueland, who currently serves as deputy director for management at the Office of Management and Budget. The White House submitted ethics paperwork on Ueland — required for nominations — to the GAO, according to a source.

Industry observers note that senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., on Thursday posted notice of a committee hearing Nov. 19 to examine more than a dozen presidential nominees for executive and judicial offices, including “a nominee to be Comptroller General.”.

The post identifies by name all of the nominees except the candidate for comptroller general. The post has been filled by an acting comptroller general, Orice Williams Brown, since Gene L. Dodaro completed his 15-year term at the end of last year.

The move by Paul to short-circuit the convening of a legislative commission to recommend candidates infuriated top Democrats, who excoriated the chairman in a joint statement Wednesday night. A special bipartisan, bicameral legislative commission is supposed to recommend at least three candidates for comptroller general to the president, according to statute.

It has been revealed that homeland Security Committee GOP staff solicited recommendations for a comptroller general from some Democratic congressional offices Wednesday afternoon, imposing a deadline of 8 a.m. Thursday, according to Democratic aides.

The president nominates the head of the GAO, the investigative arm of Congress, with the advice and consent of the Senate.

It has been revealed that paul pushed back on the criticism Thursday, saying, “Democrats have known about this for months and months and months.” He said the last time the special commission made recommendations for the office, when Barack Obama was president, “Democrats submitted their own list, Republicans submitted their own list. So they can complain all they want but they just need to make their list and submit it.”.

In the past, however, the special commission convened, sought applications for the position, interviewed candidates and deliberated before sending recommendations to the president.

A 1980 law states that when there is a vacancy in the comptroller general position, “there is established a commission to recommend individuals to the President for appointment to the vacant office,” and that the commission must submit at least three names.

Under the statute, the commission includes the speaker, Senate majority and minority leaders, House majority and minority leaders, chairs and ranking members of the Senate Homeland Security and House Oversight and Government Reform committees, and the Senate president pro tempore.

It has been revealed that in 1981, for example, after the law took effect, the two congressional leaders, Speaker Thomas P. “Tip” O’Neill Jr., D-Mass., and Senate Majority Leader Howard H. Baker, R-Tenn., sent a letter to President Ronald Reagan saying the special commission had met and voted to recommend eight candidates to succeed Comptroller General Elmer Staats.

“The members of the Commission have taken their statutory responsibility seriously,” they wrote.

Industry observers note that reagan nominated Charles A. Bowsher, who was on the list, and he was confirmed.

After Bowsher’s term ended in 1996, the commission eventually formed, interviewed multiple candidates, and deliberated for several months. Republicans controlled both chambers, and Bill Clinton was president. The members of the commission could not reach agreement, and as a result, the Republicans on the committee submitted their list to Clinton, and the Democrats on the panel submitted theirs.

Clinton also had his own list. Clinton nominated David M. Walker, who was on all three lists, and he was confirmed by the Senate more than two years after Bowsher’s departure. Walker argued Thursday against short-circuiting the commission process.

“The position is of critical importance and the related statutory Commission process should not be circumvented," Walker mentioned. "Doing so would undercut the credibility of the person and the effectiveness of the GAO.”.

Industry observers note that walker resigned in March of 2008, when George W. Bush was still president. He appointed Dodaro as acting comptroller general when he left. The commission got going several months later, creating a website with application instructions and candidate questions.

Recent findings suggest that over the next two years, the commission interviewed some 20 candidates. Democrats and Republicans on the panel were unable to reach agreement, and Democrats, who had a majority on the commission, submitted their own list to Obama in 2010. Republicans followed up with their list.

“The Commission has been working in earnest on this undertaking for more than one year and has dedicated considerable time and effort to present you with highly qualified candidates for this notable position,” then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., and then-Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid, D-Nev., along with other Democratic leaders, wrote to Obama when they submitted the Democrats’ list.

In a recent development, the Democrats’ move drew a rebuke from Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, who was ranking member of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee at the time.

Collins said in a statement she was “extremely disappointed” that Democrats “abruptly ended the selection process for the next Comptroller General without a bipartisan agreement” on the recommendations. “We have had several exceptionally qualified individuals apply to be the next leader of the GAO, and it should have been possible to come up with a consensus list.”.

Obama nominated and the Senate confirmed Dodaro, who was one of four recommendations from the Democrats.

It has been revealed that waiting more than two hours for your checked bag is frustrating. Watching it emerge covered in a brown substance that looks like human waste is considerably worse. That is what American Airlines passengers reported in Atlanta this week, though the airline states the mess had a much less revolting explanation: peanut butter.

Passengers aboard American Airlines flight 2609 from Miami (MIA) to Atlanta (ATL) on November 16, 2026, reported an unpleasant surprise at baggage claim. Travelers waited more than two hours before their luggage appeared on carousel eight at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport. When the bags arrived, passengers saw a brown substance smeared across them and naturally feared the worst.

Passenger Derick McCallum recorded the scene and later questioned the airline’s explanation:.

“Even if somebody did pack peanut butter? How much peanut butter does somebody pack to cover that many bags?”.

(my mind goes to Diddy Combs and AstroGlide…).

American later noted that liquefied peanut butter had leaked from a passenger’s checked bag, affecting nearby luggage. The airline said an environmental inspection confirmed its explanation.

“Unfortunately, a food item from a customer’s checked bag leaked during the flight, affecting several bags nearby.”.

Sources indicate that I would certainly prefer peanut butter to the alternative passengers feared. But I would still be rather unhappy about finding someone else’s sandwich spread having spoiled my suitcase.

It isn’t clear how much peanut butter was involved, how it was packaged, or exactly how it spread…feel free to speculate.

Passengers complained they were left cleaning their luggage with disinfecting wipes and tissues. American apologized and mentioned it would work directly with affected customers to resolve the situation. Since the baggage was delayed two hours anyway, did the stuff look even worse before? I check bags when necessary, particularly when traveling with my family. But stories like this reinforce why I prefer to keep my belongings with me when possible. Even if you carefully pack your own suitcase, you have no control over what someone else puts in theirs. While that’s true in a shared overhead bin too, it’s much less likely to be a problem.

There is some dark humor in a baggage carousel full of passengers trying to determine whether what that brown stuff was all over their bag, but I’m sure there was nothing to laugh about if that was your bag covered in brown.

  • The Trump administration had asked the justices to review a decision by the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the border wall is seen in 2021 stretching along the U.S.-Mexico border near Columbus, N.M. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

The Supreme Court agreed on Friday to hear a challenge to President Donald Trump’s claims that an “invasion” at the southern border can be used to deny asylum claims by refugees.

The Trump administration had asked the justices to review a decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit that held the president could not broadly deny asylum claims under federal law. The case is the latest high-profile fight over one of Trump’s signature domestic policies.

The administration argues in its petition for the justices to take the case that the president has broad authority over asylum claims, which includes shutting down the system entirely because he has decided he will not grant any.

According to recent reports, “The proclamation thus lawfully suspends access to asylum, which is a purely discretionary benefit. The court of appeals’ insistence that aliens are entitled to file futile asylum applications elevates empty procedures over substance,” the petition says.

Recent findings suggest that trump issued the order on his first day in office, declaring an “invasion” on the southern border and using that as a reason to deny asylum claims by refugees who present themselves there. The order is still in place, preventing asylum claims at the U.S.-Mexico border while the lawsuit plays out.

In court filings asking the justices to take the case, the administration pointed to “dramatic” reductions in illegal border crossings, which freed up resources to combat human trafficking and other threats.

In Friday’s order, the justices agreed to hear arguments over the legality of Trump’s executive order as well as whether the lower-court judge could grant an order in favor of all asylum seekers rather than just the ones who brought the suit.

According to recent reports, immigration rights groups initially challenged the order and won a successful ruling from a federal judge in Washington. The administration later appealed to the D.C. Circuit, where it lost at a three-judge panel before it brought the case before the justices.

It has been revealed that the D.C. Circuit held that although federal law provides a president discretion in denying asylum claims, he cannot do so categorically.

In a recent development, the ACLU and immigrant rights groups who brought the case defended the ruling in their own filing. The filing argues that Congress mandated the creation of the asylum system and the president “may not invent by fiat a newly introduced removal system that eviscerates the protections Congress mandated by statute.”.

Last term the justices ruled in favor of a separate policy dating to the first Trump administration that allowed officials to prevent asylum claims by stopping refugees from actually reaching the U.S. border.

A ruling in favor of the refugees could allow the administration to restart that policy and still deny asylum claims.

Recent findings suggest that the case granted Friday is the latest high-profile immigration policy clash on the justices’ docket this term. Earlier this year the justices agreed to hear a challenge to the administration’s policy that most immigrants facing deportation should be detained without bond.

The justices will likely hear oral arguments and decide the case granted Friday before the end of the court’s term next June.

It has been revealed that the case is Mullin v. Refugee and Immigrant Center for Education and Legal Services.

Recent findings suggest that previously, the Sapphire Reserve card offered a steady point redemption opportunity directly on Chase Travel at 1.5 cents per point (100,000 points would cover $1500, etc). But with the new version, some travel purchases you want to redeem for will either offer less value than before, the same, or more, with this new ‘Points Boost’ at 2 cents per point. We like more!

It has been revealed that I am in New York and wanted to do a little staycation, so I fired up Chase Travel and found one of my more reliable upper mid-scale hotels, The Thompson Central Park was on as part of ‘The Edit’. My two options became a very clear singular, third option.

According to recent reports, typically, I’d consider paying cash or transferring my points from Chase to Hyatt to pay for a stay like this. Hyatt has “fixed” points rates, meaning the points price is largely irrespective of the cash price and only changes by seasonal dates. For this season, it was 25,000 points per night for the Thompson Central Park.

Industry observers note that if I were to transfer my points, I’d get a free night (the cash rate was around $500) and have a really solid points redemption at exactly two cents per point. I’m not loyal to any hotel chain really, so I wouldn’t get any breakfast or “elite” benefits, but a free night is a free night.

BUT — Chase Travel had a ‘Points Boost’ option to book the hotel directly on their platform and not transfer points to Hyatt. Chase Travel was offering this property for circa 25,000 points and that would cover the $500 cash rate, but unlike transferring points to Hyatt, because I was redeeming a ‘The Edit’ property on Chase Travel, I’d receive….

It has been revealed that yep, by NOT transferring my points (and dealing with the fractured transfer journey) I was able to get myself basically $200 in additional value added to my stay with the breakfast and $100 property credit, not factoring in the value of late check out or a category room upgrade. In addition, I’ll be able to earn elite nights and Hyatt Points on the stay.

A mere 25,000 Chase Ultimate Rewards Points got me a “free” $500 hotel night, breakfast for two, and $100 to spend at the hotel. That’s a pretty stunning redemption, giving more than two cents per point of value and still allowing me to earn on the stay, unlike when you transfer your points to a loyalty program. I wish I could’ve stayed longer.

For the first time I can remember, transferring points to Hyatt was not the best option here and that’s something to stand up and take notice of.

Industry observers note that if Chase can keep up this Points Boost game, it can really send ripples through rewards. For the first time, people can easily receive tremendous value for their points through a credit card portal while still earning elite status and points with the hotel or airline of their choosing.

You can check out the newly introduced 100,000 point + 500 travel credit offer for the Sapphire Reserve. It’s 200,000 points for Sapphire Reserve Business Cards.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The agreement connects French Bee’s international network with Southwest’s extensive domestic network in the U.S.
  • French Bee also flies to Newark, Newly introduced Jersey, but Southwest does not offer service there.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Southwest and French Bee are joining forces to expand international travel options for passengers not only on both sides of the Atlantic, but also the Pacific. The two carriers unveiled a latest interline partnership that will allow travelers to combine flights on both airlines under a single ticket.

The agreement connects French Bee’s international network with Southwest’s extensive domestic network in the U.S. The partnership will provide connections through French Bee’s three U.S. gateway airports that Southwest also serves: Los Angeles, Miami, and San Francisco.

French Bee also flies to Newark, Newly introduced Jersey, but Southwest does not offer service there.

Passengers will be able to connect between French Bee’s international flights and Southwest domestic flights without having to purchase separate tickets for each airline or recheck bags at each airline.

French Bee operates an all-Airbus A350 fleet, with its primary hub located at Paris-Orly Airport, and operations to North America and destinations in the Indian Ocean and South Pacific.

According to recent reports, southwest passengers will gain access to French Bee destinations not only from Paris, but also Tahiti in French Polynesia, which the French carrier flies to from San Francisco. The partnership will also offer one-stop French Bee connections from Paris to the Maldives and Sri Lanka, scheduled to launch in December 2026, along with current flights to Reunion Island.

According to recent reports, for French Bee customers, the upcoming arrangement provides access to a much larger network of domestic destinations throughout the U.S. Southwest’s network includes cities such as Las Vegas, Chicago, Dallas, Denver, Nashville, Austin, San Diego, Phoenix, and multiple destinations in the Hawaiian Islands.

The agreement represents another step in Southwest’s expanding international connectivity strategy, as the airline continues to develop relationships with overseas carriers rather than rely exclusively on its own international operations with its all-Boeing 737 fleet.

Tickets for connecting flights are now available through French Bee’s website.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rep. Lauren Boebert, R-Colo., leaves the Capitol after a vote on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

According to recent reports, colorado Rep. Lauren Boebert, an outspoken conservative and Second Amendment provocateur, lost her bid for a fourth term to Democrat Eileen Laubacher, a retired rear admiral in the Navy.

Laubacher was leading 48.8 percent to 47.9 percent, a margin of 3,441 votes, when The Associated Press called the race on Friday.

Recent findings suggest that the red-hued 4th District, which spreads across eastern Colorado, was unexpectedly competitive this year, a sign of how deep into red turf Democrats were able to compete this year. Boebert had Donald Trump’s endorsement, but her relationship with the president has been strained at times after she began pressing for the release of files related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Laubacher proved to be a strong fundraiser, hauling in $13.7 million as of mid-October to Boebert’s $1.2 million.

Boebert has been one of the most visible and controversial members of the House GOP conference since she won an upset primary in the 3rd District over five-term incumbent Republican Scott Tipton in 2020.

Industry observers note that A newcomer to electoral politics, she rapidly positioned herself as a disruptor on Capitol Hill, heckling former President Joe Biden during his 2022 State of the Union address and tangling with a fellow GOP firebrand, former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene of Georgia, on the House floor.

In 2023, Boebert was embroiled in an embarrassing incident in a Denver theater that was captured on surveillance video. She subsequently embarked on an apology tour.

In a recent development, running for reelection the first time in the 3rd District, which is centered around Colorado’s rural Western Slope, Boebert barely won a closer-than-expected race against Democrat Adam Frisch in 2022. When Frisch confirmed he was trying again in 2024, Boebert switched to the 4th District, which had been considered far friendlier terrain for the GOP.

According to recent reports, this year, Democrats won all of Colorado’s House seats, except in the 3rd District, which is held by Rep. Jeff Hurd.

Mary Ellen McIntire contributed to this report.

On Tour: Australian Indie Darling Radio Free Alice on Tour Life, Guerrilla Gigs, and American Motels

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1763 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This article is part of a newly introduced series, On Tour, in which we talk to touring artists about life on the road.
  • On Halloween, a bouncing crowd of skateboarders, witches, ghosts, and ghouls slowly coalesced in New York City's Tompkins Square Park.
  • Sources indicate that that’s what makes the album title so apt: The young Aussies are caught between cities and countries, trying to make sense of everyday life while the road itself starts to feel like home.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This article is part of a newly introduced series, On Tour, in which we talk to touring artists about life on the road.

On Halloween, a bouncing crowd of skateboarders, witches, ghosts, and ghouls slowly coalesced in New York City's Tompkins Square Park. They were there for a quintessentially East Village pop-up concert headlined by the Melbourne-based post-punk band Radio Free Alice (followed by an after party at Niagara). The band's debut album, What’s In Between, was just released the day prior, blending the high energy of ’80s new wave with biting social satire and a healthy dose of cheek. Having picked up a following in Australia and Europe, the four-piece group has built an underground reputation on guerrilla gigs like this one—held everywhere from beneath London railway bridges and Melbourne’s former Pentridge Prison to suburban backyards in Austin, Texas.

Sources indicate that that’s what makes the album title so apt: The young Aussies are caught between cities and countries, trying to make sense of everyday life while the road itself starts to feel like home. They’re in the thick of their own coming-of-age story, and one that's unfolding on an international stage. Fresh off the first dates of a nearly sold-out European lineup, tickets are now on sale for their What's In Between North America tour, which will kick off in San Francisco on February 24, 2027.

Industry observers note that earlier this month, vocalist and guitarist Noah Learmonth picked up my call from a Sprinter van somewhere in Germany, on the road from Copenhagen to Berlin. With the wit, gumption, and on-stage vocals of a Gen-Z Morrissey, his devilish grin fills the screen as he tells me he spends 99% of his time in the window seat behind the van’s little table, facing forward. His preferred seat is at the moment occupied by guitarist Jules Paradiso. He gives me a 360-degree tour of their ecosystem, where everyone has settled into their own version of life on the road. Drummer Lochie Dowd has claimed a small sleeping nook near the back. Michael Phillips, bassist and resident reader, sits with his Kindle, having just finished Christos Tsiolkas’s The Slap. As for who’s running the show? “Fuck, no one,” the still-grinning Noah says. “There’s a man up front called Ben, our tour manager, who’s a crazy man. He’s the one who leads the blind. We’d all be fucked otherwise.”.

What’s everyone’s travel personality on tour? Who’s running the show?

Recent findings suggest that yeah, [I'm] type D. I’m sort of in my own world when I’m traveling—headphones on, that kind of vibe. Jules is really easy manufacturer. He’s a valuable asset to have in the world. Michael’s pretty chill, too. He’s looking at me now as I summarize his personality. Lochie likes to sleep in this little nook. That’s a major part of his tour experience: finding that little nook.

It has been revealed that when we met Ben, we just fell in love with him and his crazy methods, his madness. The thing about Ben is he gets our sound right every time. It’s really annoying when someone else does the sound and you watch the videos back and go, ‘Oh my God, what the fuck? Why is there no bass in the synth? Why do we sound like Duran Duran? What’s going on? I sound like Sonic Youth.’ That’s not at all what we were going for. Two of my favorite bands, though. But Ben gets exactly the sound we’re going for, and he’s a real empath. We’ve spent so much time on the road together. He’s our guy.

Where do you stay while you're on the road?

Sources indicate that when we’re touring Europe, we’ll stay in budget hotels. Either an Ibis or a Travelodge. In America, it’s more motel-type places—Motel 6 kind of things. It’s very cliché, but kind of sick in a way. Each morning when you wake up, you set your alarm for half an hour before you have to leave, get up, have a shower, smash your clothes into your backpack, and run down to the lobby so you’re not late and Ben doesn’t give you a verbal spanking.

According to recent reports, terrible. I just had McDonald’s. I don’t even like McDonald’s. You literally don’t have an option. You pull into a service station and the only food there is McDonald’s. Jules is a Major Mac guy, though. I know that.

I’m personally notoriously light. I just have this yellow North Face backpack that I’ve had since I was about seven years old. My auntie gave it to me for my birthday. My trusty yellow backpack. Lochie has a significant suitcase, Michael has a smaller suitcase, and Jules has a big, backpacker-style backpack.

Essentials you can’t tour without?

I’m wearing the same jeans I’ve been wearing every day for the past year. I got them from a thrift shop in Melbourne. So my essentials are my jeans. Lochie’s are his headphones—we all use Sony. Jules’s is…video games. He’d hate that I just said that. Let’s say his laptop. Michael’s is his Kindle. He’s the best reader. Let’s see what he’s reading…ah, he just finished The Slap.

What's your favorite city that you've played in so far?

Upcoming York. I mean, the obvious answer is New York. New York’s the best city in the fucking world. It’s amazing.

In a recent development, the first few times we were there, we partied a lot. We just remarked, ‘This is a fucking adult amusement park.’ It’s ridiculous. We were staying with this band called Been Stellar, too, who are great. When we’re back we like going out on the Lower East Side, especially to this bar called Treasure Club. I personally also love the diners. I think the atmosphere in an old-school, family-run diner might be the best atmosphere of any place in the world.

Favorite venue you’ve ever played?

A gig is just people playing music, and it can happen literally anywhere. There are no rules. You can do it anywhere. Shaking up the gig setting—rethinking what a gig is and what it can feel like—is really fun, and it keeps it notable. The Melbourne set at Pentridge Prison [a former 19th century prison that's been transformed into a residential area] was sick. It was an incredible visual.

What about a city that surprised you?

Industry observers note that zurich. So random. I just remember having a strangely amazing time. I remember leaving that gig thinking, ‘Actually, there was something incredibly awesome and sweet about that.’ And it was the people. They were just these thoughtful, sweet people.

Industry observers note that after a show like Zurich, we’ll be in the green room after. We’ll probably crack open a beer, and Lochie will be funny. If it went really, really well, we might go out somewhere nearby, to a pub or a bar or something. But generally, what happens is we go back to the green room, we’re really buzzed, we’ll have a beer and we’ll be pretty hyped up. Then Ben will come in and say, ‘All hands on deck. We need to load up the van. We’ve got to get to the next city.’ Zurich, though—I’d love to do it again.

What's your impression of the United States so far?

According to recent reports, I mean, there’s one thing about America: the difference between, say, New York and LA, and then LA and Minneapolis or somewhere, is worlds apart. You could be in completely different countries.

According to recent reports, middle America can feel like an absolute time warp. When you’re on the road, there’s a sort of repetitiveness to the long stretches of road that all seem to look exactly the same. You arrive at a petrol station that’s identical to the last one you stopped at. There’s that stereotype that Americans are massive talkers, but I’ve found that’s almost underrated. I can’t believe how chatty Americans are. They love just talking, going on and on. Coming from Australia, it’s the opposite. I love it.

Any memories you've made on the road that you’ll never forget?

In a recent development, the first time we played in LA, this very sweet girl called Alice randomly made us all these gifts. She gave us all these handmade things: embroidered bracelets with band-related names and glasses with our names on them. I find something quite American about that. It’s just so sweet. In Europe, people tend to be a little less expressive in that way. It’s still just amazing to me.

Recent findings suggest that glasgow had this sort of “rara”-ness to it, which was really fun and funny for us. It just felt so boisterous. We’d play a slower song, and they’d still find a way to just absolutely lose their minds. It was cute.

When you're not on tour, where’s home for you guys?

In a recent development, nowhere, not really anywhere. I’m not exaggerating. I feel disingenuous calling anywhere our home at this point. But if there were one, it would be London. It’s making a substantial impression on us. What’s cool is that, a year before we moved to London, we played to maybe one person at one of our gigs there. Then, the following year, we played to this really big, sold-out room. It was an incredibly high-energy, adrenaline-fueled, amazing, crazy show. That was special. I’ll never forget it. It was probably my favorite show.

It has been revealed that there are so many young indie-rock bands coming up in London that I’m seeing, and they’re all ambitious and exciting. I’m really excited by London. It’s lived up to the hopes I had for it. Because of that we’ve found ourselves hanging out at venues like the Shacklewell Arms and the George Tavern, that sort of thing.

While you're on tour, what do you miss the most?

You know, this isn’t a very cool answer, and I kind of wish it were, but the truth is I really miss having an exercise routine. In Melbourne, I was really massive on swimming every morning, doing laps or going to the gym. I find it puts me in a really good place for the day. I’m chill and focused, not neurotic, and I just find it’s really good for me.

What's a band touring right now that you are personally excited about?

Industry observers note that lime Garden. They’re an all female lineup. The English rock scene is a bit of a sausage fest, so they’re a breath of fresh air.

Review: Air France Hop! Embraer 170 Business Class (BSL-CDG)

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

My trip to Fresh York on Air France began with a short domestic flight on the Embraer 170 in business class from Basel to Paris, a short and pleasant journey.

Years ago after my La Premiere flight from Los Angeles to Paris, I continued on to Basel on an Embraer 190 in what Air France marketed as business class. But the service onboard was no different than economy class: there was no blocked middle seat, meal, or beverages served in glass..it was just regular economy class service.

But Air France has come a long way and I feel like even on a short domestic business class flight it really has really raised the bar in terms of service.

I booked my ticket from Basel to Fresh York JFK via Paris for 60,000 Flying Blue miles and $453 in business class, booking just 36 hours prior to departure (so yes, Air France does release last-minute award space).

Basel Airport straddles Switzerland and France. I entered on the French side and checked in for my flight.

On the check-in level you can walk back and forth freely between the French and Swiss side, but on the lower level and upper level there’s a physical barrier. For example, I went out to the terrace on the upper level and there’s a fence separating the two nations.

After visiting the Skyview Lounge, now operated by Aspire, I headed to the gate for boarding at 1:45 pm, which began right on schedule.

Stepping onboard, I found my seat in 2F.

According to recent reports, the aircraft has 76 seats in a 2-2 configuration. Each seat has 31 inches of pitch and is 18 inches wide. Seats recline three inches. There are individual air vents, but no power of any kind: neither USB or a universal power socket.

Recent findings suggest that business class can be adjusted according to demand, the “genius” of having the same seat. On today’s flight there were three rows of business class, but only three passengers: we each had our own row. Air France now blocks adjacent seats in business class, so that is a substantial advantage versus economy class.

The only other business class distinctive was that each seat had a pillow and water bottle:.

At only 250 miles, there wasn’t  much time for a meal service.

According to recent reports, air France nevertheless offers business class passengers a small meal box on its shorthaul network, part of a catering concept introduced in 2024 and developed with Servair Corporate Chef François Adamski, a Bocuse d’Or winner and Meilleur Ouvrier de France. For flights departing after 10:00 am, Air France serves what it calls a “signature” sandwich along with a French sweet or dessert, with the selection changing regularly. It is served in a sturdy cardboard box.

In a recent development, on my flight, the meal consisted of two finger sandwiches with smoked salmon and a creamy herb filling on brown bread, along with a small pecan tart and a chocolate…a very nice treat. The airline also serves wine and Champagne in proper glassware, though I just had sparkling water on this flight.

> Read More: Air France Served This Surprisingly Elegant Business Class Meal On A 250-Mile Flight.

Flight attendants onboard were very polite and efficient: meals and drinks were offered immediately and refills offered after they had completed service in economy class and again before landing, all on a very short flight.

This flight has no internet and no in-flight-entertainment, but Starlink is coming to these jets.

However, it was a beautiful day tempearture wise and I enjoyed looking out the window, especially as we flew over Paris (thought it was a bit hazy) as we neared CDG.

Business class passengers have a dedicated lavatory in the font of the cabin. It was small but clean.

We landed on time in Paris where I ran into a fairly complicated connection to Terminal 2E Hall M…but it was a short but lovely flight.

#99923. I Walked Solo Along England’s Rugged South West Coast Path for Three Days

I Walked Solo Along England’s Rugged South West Coast Path for Three Days

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1637 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’m standing atop a spit of land jutting out into the English Channel, peering down at a beach accessible only by boat, where a small group of sunbathers lounge on the rocky sand.
  • I was nearing the end of the first day of a three-day solo walking trip along a slice of England’s South West Coast Path, a 630-mile trail through some of the country’s most beautiful land- and seascapes.
  • Since tackling an admittedly easier two-day walk from Dover to Sandwich the previous summer, I’d become totally enamored with England’s coastal paths.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’m standing atop a spit of land jutting out into the English Channel, peering down at a beach accessible only by boat, where a small group of sunbathers lounge on the rocky sand. The view is a welcome excuse to catch my breath before continuing along five more rolling cliffs—400 steep feet up, 400 steep feet down, and repeat. And so, despite my exhausted legs and the blister that’s forming over my right major toe, I decide to imprint this impossibly peaceful scene into my brain to remind myself why I’m doing this trip.

Dorset's limestone Jurassic Coast.

I was nearing the end of the first day of a three-day solo walking trip along a slice of England’s South West Coast Path, a 630-mile trail through some of the country’s most beautiful land- and seascapes. Earlier this year, it became part of the newly created King Charles III England Coast Path, inaugurated with a brisk March walk by the king himself (wearing a suit, natch). The route now incorporates all of England’s preexisting regional coastal paths, adding upcoming sections to create a wider network that stretches across nearly 2,700 miles, giving walkers a chance to access parts of the country far beyond the typical travel itinerary.

Since tackling an admittedly easier two-day walk from Dover to Sandwich the previous summer, I’d become totally enamored with England’s coastal paths. I realized I could experience so much more of the country’s most beautiful landscapes by foot than I ever could by train or car. For my second foray, I chose one of the more frequented set of trails: walking east from Weymouth to Bournemouth across Dorset. This stretch is known for its incredible rock formations, the result of millions of years of waves washing against the coast. That erosion has also led to the discovery of some of the world’s oldest fossils—giving the region the name of Jurassic Coast.

A view of the South West coast Path's rugged countryside, which is now more easily accessible to hikers thanks to the wider newly created King Charles III England Coast Path.

Recent findings suggest that when I’d set off five hours earlier from the charming seaside town of Weymouth—a destination made popular by King George III’s multiple visits at the turn of the 19th century—the going had been easy. My only roadblock was a military parade that a British historical society couldn’t have arranged any better: an Army band marched in front of a stretch of beach-facing Georgian townhouses as Union Jack bunting fluttered in the sea breeze. An Anglican priest delivered a short prayer. There was a Spitfire flyover. If you ignored all the iPhones and mobility scooters, it was a scene that would have fit in comfortably 80 years ago.

Sources indicate that by setting out alone on a three-day walk, I was seeking solitude, and moments like that clifftop break, when I had the view all to myself, delivered. But the long way out of the Weymouth hubbub also clarified why walking England’s coastal paths is so approachable—especially for those of us who love the outdoors but want to sleep indoors. Since the country is quite densely populated, you can easily walk the trails from town to town, and hotel to hotel, without the weight (and stress) of camping equipment. For those same reasons, it’s also perfect as a solo walker; the risks feel more manageable when you know medical care is within reach; that you’re rarely without phone service; and that your hotel door locks at night.

According to recent reports, after 12 miles or so of walking, I arrived at West Lulworth, a town of centuries-old stone cottages that can best be described as “quaint.” I was greeted by the famous Durdle Door, a limestone arch that snakes out of a cliff and into the Channel, with clusters of beachgoers splashing underneath. It's a place worth lingering: After going down my final descent of the day, I snuck a peek at Lulworth Cove, a popular bay almost fully enclosed by limestone (and a UNESCO World Heritage Site), before checking into the Old Barn Inn, a B&B up the road for a gloriously hot shower.

A view of Durdle Door, a limestone arch that can be seen from the trail.

Industry observers note that my second day of walking presented a new challenge: Part of my planned route was closed because it crossed a firing range in use by the Army for training. To avoid it, I rode the bus (the Jurassic Coast is very well served by public transit, at least in summer) part of the way to my next destination, then planned to take a shortcut through some fields to get back to the coast. Sarah, the owner of the Old Barn, had given me extremely specific verbal directions based on local landmarks, which were easy enough to follow until I’d reached the “horrible hill” she warned me of. It was then that I realized I was in the middle of a field with no obvious path out. I bushwhacked to a nearby road, the peace of solitude nowhere to be found as I muttered, “I’ve done this to myself.”.

But thanks to my two puny bars of cell phone service, I navigated over another field, through a herd of sheep, along a ravine, and then emerged, alarmingly sweaty, into the absolutely charming limestone village of Worth Matravers. I made a beeline to the local pub (as recommended by Sarah), and enjoyed what was undoubtedly the best pint of my life looking out over a grassy field—and to the ocean beyond. As I sipped my lager at a picnic table, a forceful summer wind whipped off the water, knocking down the pub’s sandwich board advertising Cornish pasties, but it didn’t bother me or the handful of other pubgoers sitting out in the sun.

Perhaps there is something to the old saying about victory being sweetest after you’ve known defeat, because for all of the frustration I endured that day, the second half of my walk was absolutely breathtaking. After an easy, peaceful meander back down to the coastal path, I spent the next two hours walking through clifftop fields where I saw more deer and cows than humans, and past the famous Danding Ledge, a stone shelf jutting into a patch of sea popular with wild swimming enthusiasts. The wind that had teased me earlier died down closer to the water, and all I could hear was the crash of the waves against the rocks below. When I’ve needed a moment of peace in the few months since then, I’ve summoned the memory of that afternoon and the calm those clifftop fields offered.

A solo walker making their way along the South West Coast Path.

I woke up the following morning in the seaside town of Swanage with calves so sore that the thought of any incline made me nervous. To my dismay, I discovered right away that, to pick up the coastal path from the inn where I’d stayed (Rivendell Guest House), I first had to climb a steep staircase from the sandy beach, up the cliff to the bluff. Thankfully, shortly thereafter things flattened out. It was also the busiest section of the trail I encountered—though, even here, I saw only a dozen or so people, mostly locals in athletic gear out for a morning ramble.

In a recent development, when I reached the hilltop, I was greeted by a few hundred cows—and just beyond their enclosure, the Old Harry Rocks came into view. Millions of years’ worth of waves have chiseled away at this promontory, carving a series of chalk stacks that now sit away from the mainland. I watched two ambitious kayakers appear on the side of the rocks where the water was calmer and stare up at the feat of nature—enjoying a perspective that I’m sure is heavily advised against, and which only few have gotten to enjoy.

The final part of my walk was along Studland Beach, a sandy four-mile stretch that backs up onto a nature preserve. I waded into the water, sat in the sun, and saw a boat selling ice cream delight children up and down the crowded beach, before reaching the last mile—which also happens to be home to the UK’s most popular naturist (or nudist) beach. The ice cream boat pulled up again, and it tickled me to see that the evenly tanned sexagenarians were just as pleased to have a midday treat as the energetic children I'd just passed.

Boats bob in the water near Old Harry Rocks in Studland, Dorset.

It has been revealed that the final adventure of my trip also brought out childish delight in me: To get to Bournemouth, where I’d catch a train back to London, I had to take a four-minute ferry ride. Alongside me on the ferry was a double-decker bus with its upper deck open to the elements, letting passengers take full advantage of the beach breeze. The sheer logistics of this was a thrill to witness: a convertible bus driving onto a boat.

According to recent reports, on the other side of the strait, I got onto that very bus—aptly called The Breezer—and watched as the natural coastline was slowly enveloped by an urban milieu. It was a slightly rude awakening to reemerge into Bournemouth, a small university city where the asphalt had soaked up the sun, presaging the upcoming heatwave. But I realized as I walked through the train station that I was inadvertently grinning with pride. I assumed no one would ask me, a stinky and visibly sweaty woman, what I’d been up to, but if they had, I would have been all too happy to tell them about my solo walk along the South West Coast Path.

Former Washington Rep. Jim McDermott dies at 89
